articleTitle: Feasibility study of an unbalanced MACKEY type R with enhanced robustness on metal
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A meta-surface-inspired antenna chip developed by KIT EOE Laboratory (MACKEY), which operates not only in free space but also on a metal plate, is proposed. In this study, an unbalanced MACKEY using an inverted L-shaped antenna as the feed element is proposed. In addition, to improve the characteristics of unbalanced MACKEY on metals, an unbalanced MACKEY type R is proposed with an optimized antenna width.

articleTitle: Conjoined, Wi-Fi 6E MIMO Antennas for Laptops
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A coupled-fed Wi-Fi 6E monopole/loop antenna, occupying a compact size of 5 mm × 14.5 mm, for 2.4/5/6 GHz wireless local area network (WLAN) operation, including the latest 6 GHz band (5925-7125 MHz), is first introduced. The antenna comprises one coupling strip and one parasitic strip, which produce the 0.25-λ monopole resonant mode in the 2.4 GHz band and 0.5-λ monopole and 1.0-λ loop resonant modes in the 5/6 GHz bands. The single antenna design may be the smallest 2.4/5/6 GHz laptop antenna in the recent literature. Furthermore, by conjoining the parasitic strips of the two said antennas and embedding a decoupling capacitor therein, two decoupled (multi-input multi-output) MIMO antennas can be attained.

articleTitle: A WLAN/WiFi-6E MIMO Antenna Design for Handset Devices
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a six-antenna design for handset devices. The antenna comes with multiple operation bands that cover the two conventional WLAN bands, which extends from 2400 to 2484 MHz and 5150 to 5925 MHz, as well as the newly added WiFi-6E band that covers the 5925 to 7125 MHz band. The proposed antenna geometry comprises three elements. A printed planar monopole serves as the driven element. A parasitic strip is placed alongside with the monopole. A dual-branch shorted element, which contains an inverted L branch and an inverted C branch, is placed right next to the driving monopole. These structures help excite multiple resonances to form a broad operation band and to improve the matching performance. Simulation results show that the proposed MIMO antenna array has good impedance matching and decoupling performances in the desired WiFi bands.

articleTitle: Asymmetrical, Self-Isolated Laptop Antenna in the 2.4/5/6 GHz Wi-Fi 6E Bands
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An asymmetrical, self-isolated antenna capable of 2.4/5 GHz wireless local area network (WLAN) operation with the new 6 GHz (5925-7125 MHz) band in the laptop computer is presented. The design is formed on a substrate of size 30 mm × 6 mm. By first offset feeding the 2.4 GHz symmetrical loop, a well-matched wideband at 7 GHz can be obtained. With incorporating the meandered tuning portion in the loop’s side strip, two higher-order modes are lowered and combined to cover the 5150-7125 GHz bands. For multi-input multi-output (MIMO) applications, arranging two antennas symmetrically with a spacing of 4 mm is also analyzed. The transmission coefficients (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>) and envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) of the antennas are good.

articleTitle: Realistic Interference Simulations in a Data Center Offering Wireless Communication at Low Terahertz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the simulation of Top-of-Rack wireless links in a data center at terahertz frequencies. The propagation is simulated via ray tracing considering the effect of beam-steerable antennas. The data transmission is evaluated by link level simulations where the time-discrete interference signals are superposed at the receiver. The simulation shows that interference leads to a signal-to-interference ratio below 10dB for more than half of the links.

articleTitle: Antenna Technologies for Beyond-5G Wireless Communication: Challenges and Opportunities
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper provides an overview of the Sweden-Taiwan collaborative research framework project ‘Antenna Technologies for Beyond-5G Wireless Communication’ that has been recently established to develop robust and energy-efficient integrated antenna solutions for frequencies beyond 100 GHz as future enabling technologies for the 5G+ applications. Technological challenges in manufacturing and integration with electronics as well as available opportunities are discussed.

articleTitle: Novel Circuit-Shape Leaky Wave Waveguide for Microwave Snow melting
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In a snow melting device using microwaves, it is generally necessary to install some waveguides each with a power source in order to melt snow in a planar area. This paper proposes a novel leaky wave slotted waveguide that is constructed in a circuit shape to achieve uniform snow melting for an area with a single microwave power-supply device with low cost. The behavior of the electromagnetic field in the proposed structure, in which the electromagnetic waves radiated from the feeding point go around the waveguide and return, was analyzed using the FDTD method. The electrical characteristics of the proposed waveguide simulated with parameterized position of the feeding point and the slot spacing were compared. The results clarified that the electric field strength in the upper surface direction of the waveguide increase when the slot spacing was set to the guide wavelength and the feeding point was located at the end in the longitudinal direction of the circuit.

articleTitle: Design of Laptop Antenna for WLAN and Wi-Fi 6E Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a monopole slot antenna applied to the metal ground plane of a laptop computer/notebook. The planar size of the proposed slot antenna is 27×10 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and it is built on a FR4 substrate with a thickness of 0.8 mm. The proposed slot antenna is composed of a couple-feed line and two dissimilar monopole slots, in which the two slots can generate the WLAN 2.4 GHz (2400-2484 MHz) and WLAN 5 GHz (5150-5875 MHz) operational bands. Furthermore, the proposed slot antenna can also cover the recent Wi-Fi 6E operational band that covers the frequency range from 5925 to 7125 MHz.

articleTitle: Design of MIMO Antennas for WiFi/5G Small Cell Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a 4×4 MIMO antenna for small cell is presented. The proposed antenna operates at the WiFi 2.4/6E (2400~2484 MHz, 5000~7125 MHz) and 5G (3300~5000 MHz) bands. In order to excite these three bands with omnidirectional radiation and good isolation, the antenna consists of two vertical and a horizontal substrates. The vertical structure is operated at WiFi bands and is composed of PIFA and monopole antenna. The horizontal one is an element of 5G band and made up of four slot antennas with a 90 degree phase difference. Then two vertical substrates are cross-soldered to the horizontal one, a 4×4 MIMO antenna is obtained. In this way omnidirectional radiation and good isolation can be achieved. The final antenna has an overall size of 120 × 120 × 24.8 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Experimental results are in good agreement with simulated values.

articleTitle: Null Frequency Scanning Antenna Based on Asymmetric Phase Transforming of Spoof Surface Plasmon Polaritons (SSPPs)
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A null frequency scanning antenna is proposed based on the asymmetric spoof surface plasmon polaritons (SSPPs) in this paper. Dispersion property of the SSPP mode is determined by the sub-wavelength configurations, and phase constants of electromagnetic waves in SSPP mode vary nonlinearly with the frequency change. Therefore, two SSPP radiators with asymmetric phase transforming could realize frequency scanning in the boresight for either null or main lobe when magnitudes of radiated fields are the same and phase difference between two radiators is even or odd multiple of 180°. A prototype antenna is designed and simulated from 5.99 GHz to 6.44 GHz, and angular range of null scanning is from -20° to 28° is obtained with null depth over 20 dB. The proposed antenna has potential in suppressing interference and realizing frequency scanning monopulse for direction detection and locating.

articleTitle: A Millimetre-Wave Tri-Band Antenna Embedded on Smart Watch for Wearable Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a compact size patch antenna embedded on smart watch for wearable applications. The proposed antenna operates at millimeter-wave frequencies, i.e., 28 GHz, 38 GHz, and 60 GHz for wireless communication applications. A coplanar waveguide (CPW) technique is utilized in this research to keep the size compact. The proposed antenna is printed on a flexible Roger substrate RT Duroid 5880 with a standard thickness of 0.25mm. The overall size of the antenna is 4mm × 3mm × 0.25mm. We observed that the proposed antenna provides stable results when it is simulated on a watch strap along with human tissue like skin. The total radiation efficiency is more than 85% and the gain values of the proposed antenna at 28GHz, 38GHz, and 60GHz frequencies are 5.29dB, 7.47dB, and 9dB, respectively. Hence, the proposed tri-band antenna is a perfect candidate for wearable applications.

articleTitle: Single-Layer Wideband CP CPW-Fed Antenna based on Staircase-Shape Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This research proposed a single-layer wideband circularly polarized (CP) coplanar waveguide (CPW)-fed antenna based on staircase-shaped metasurface (MTS) for C-band applications. The proposed CPW-fed antenna was a single-layer, which consisted of 4 × 4 periodic staircase-shaped MTS on the upper layer, a CPW feed, and a rectangular slot ground plane on the lower layer. A linearly polarized (LP) wave was generated by a CPW with a slot ground plane and converted to a circularly polarized wave by staircase-shaped MTS elements. The dimensions of the proposed antenna were 0.54λ × 0.54λ × 0.04λ at the lowest operating frequency. The simulated results of impedance bandwidth (IBW) and axial ratio (ARBW) at the center frequency of 5.2 GHz were 67.3% (4.1 – 7.6 GHz) and 15.9% (4.8 – 5.7 GHz), respectively. The maximum gain was 5.6 dBi at 5.3 GHz. The radiation patterns of the proposed CPW-fed antenna based on staircase-shaped MTS were right-hand circular polarization (RHCP) characteristic radiation at the operating frequency.

articleTitle: A Compact D-band Transition from Rectangular Waveguide to Substrate Integrated Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A D-band transition from air-filled WR-06 rectangular waveguide to substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) is presented. The transition primarily uses an aperture-coupled patch antenna and its surrounding annular slot to transform the TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode from the WR-06 waveguide to the SIW on a printed circuit board (PCB). The simulated fractional bandwidth with |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| < − 10 dB of a single transition is 14% from 137 GHz to 158 GHz with an insertion loss of less than 0.7 dB at 150 GHz. Meanwhile, the fractional bandwidth of a back-to-back transition is 9% from 143 GHz to 157 GHz with an insertion loss 1.42 dB at 150 GHz.

articleTitle: Identification of bedsore using electromagnetic waves for a non-contact detection system
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Bedsores are injuries caused by pressure on the skin for a long time and stagnation of blood flow. The more such injuries progress, the longer the treatment period becomes. In some serious cases, surgery is required. Therefore, an early detection method is important. In this study, we develop a non-contact bedsore detection system by using electromagnetic waves. In this paper, we investigate a method using wavelet transforms to develop a more accurate bedsore detection method.

articleTitle: A New Approach to Design Microstrip Patch Antenna with Wideband Harmonic Suppression
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A new microstrip patch antenna with wideband harmonic suppression is presented in this paper. Compared to the traditional patch antenna, a dual-point feeding technique is adopted in our patch antenna design. This feeding method is able to excite the fundamental TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf> mode and control the higher order harmonics at the same time. Detailed analysis for the harmonic modes control is provided, and the performance of the antenna is simulated and optimized. It is indicated that the designed patch antenna not only has a good radiation pattern and stable gain at the working frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, but also can achieve the harmonic suppression up to 2.8f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> with resorting to the proposed dual-point feeding method. Simulated and measured results are given, well validating the feeding approach.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Automotive Antenna Over the Air Performance
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This document outlines the measurement methodology currently employed to evaluate wireless technology on vehicles. Near Field Over the Air measurement results are provided and the Figure of Merit developed to assess the performance is reviewed. Simulation results of a more complex measurement scenario are also presented.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Array Fed Reflector Architectures for Broadband Satellite Missions
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, an efficient tool to estimate the antenna system performance of Array Fed Reflector configurations is presented. Acceleration techniques are applied to the analysis of the reflector antenna to estimate the beam patterns. Then, some system parameters are evaluated once the channel characteristics are fully defined. Finally, a parametric study of the multibeam coverage is shown as an example of the capabilities of the tool. The final aim of the study is the optimization of the antenna payload in terms of system parameters such as the aggregated throughput.

articleTitle: Design of A 2-Bit Dual Linearly Polarized Reconfigurable Reflectarray Element
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel design approach for dual-polarized 2-bit reconfigurable reflectarray element is proposed. The transmission phase shifter is designed using a single-layer Jerusalem cross loaded with four PIN diodes. By spatially cascading it with a 1-bit reflective phase shifter using a Malta cross integrated with 2 PIN diodes, a 2-bit phase resolution is achieved by switching these six PIN diodes. The simulated results show that the proposed element has good performance at four phase states, where the average insertion loss is 2.2 dB at 5.8 GHz. Compared with the conventional multi-bit phase reconfigurable design, the proposed method has advantages on simple structure, low loss, and low lost.

articleTitle: High Gain Dual Parasitic Patch Loaded Wideband Antenna for 28 GHz 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work presents the design of a high gain wideband antenna for 28 GHz band application. The antenna structure was inspired from a conventional circular patch which is modified using consecutive loading of two parasitic patch. The presented antenna offers a wideband to completely cover the globally allocated band spectrum for 28 GHz 5G applications. Moreover, the broad side radiation pattern, relatively compact size and high gain makes the proposed work potential candidate for future 5G applications.

articleTitle: Measurement of 4 GHz Radio Altimeter Interference Path Loss Including 5G Sub-6 Frequency Bands Using Beechcraft B300 Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The interference path loss (IPL) is the propagation loss of the signal power transmitted from the electric devices and that received at the avionics receiving port. IPL characteristics should be known to examine the coexistence condition of avionics and other electric systems. In this study, the 4 GHz radio altimeter IPL characteristics are measured using Beechcraft B300 aircraft. To cover the frequency band of the 5G mobile communication system, the measurement frequency band is set between 3.5 and 4.5 GHz. The measured minimum IPL values inside and outside the cabin are 67.5 dB and 47.7 dB, respectively, between frequencies 3.5 and 4.1 GHz.

articleTitle: WiThRay: Versatile 3D Simulator for Intelligent Reflecting Surface-aided MmWave Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication systems that provide wideband spectra are a key technology in 5G communication systems. Although the small coverage of mmWave communication systems can be extended by beamforming with a large number of antennas, the strong directivity of signals inherited in high-frequency bands makes the mmWave communication systems vulnerable to signal blockage. Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS), which is able to change channel propagation characteristics by using a large number of passive elements, will become essential to mitigate the signal blockage in mmWave channels. Most of previous works on the mmWave systems using IRS, however, relied on stochastic channel models and did not consider real-world geometric environments. This paper is to introduce WiThRay (Wireless three-dimensional ray-tracing), a versatile simulator that generates the mmWave channels for 3D rendered geometric environments, where multiple base stations and multiple IRSs can be configured, based on ray-tracing. WiThRay also models the IRS response based on electromagnetics. Using WiThRay, we demonstrate the advantage of the IRS-aided mmWave communication systems in complicated and realistic environments.

articleTitle: Development of Circular Polarization MACKEY
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, a meta-surface-inspired antenna chip developed by the KIT EOE Laboratory (MACKEY) that is sufficiently robust to a metal object, has been proposed. The MACKEY transmits circularly polarized signals by combining multiple antennas and substrates.

articleTitle: A High Gain Narrowband Microstrip Antenna Array for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a high gain narrowband microstrip patch antenna array for wireless power transmission (WPT) applications. It is presents the design, simulation, and fabrication of microstrip patch antenna array for close-range WPT systems. Various antenna array such as single patch, 2 × 4, and 4 × 8 array antenna working at 2.45 GHz are proposed. The 4 × 8 array antenna is fabricated and measured using Anritsu 37364D Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) with anechoic chamber. To achieve a high gain improvement, a rectangular slot, and a C-shaped ring , which can eliminate the influence of the radiation from the feeding microstrip line and the ground plane on the proposed antenna. The gains range from 11.5 to 12.18 dBi in the operating band of 2.40-2.49 GHz.

articleTitle: A Design of Circular Polarization Antenna Array Using Sequential Rotation for SATCOM
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The Ka-band circular polarization sequential antenna array design is proposed. The sequential rotation technique can be used to maintain wide-band axial ratio response. The 64 elements polarized sequential array is realized with a return loss better than 10 dB in operation frequency band.

articleTitle: An Attempt of Underwater Position Estimation in Pseudo-Scale Model Using Cross-Dipole Array
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a method of using received power distribution with a 9-cross dipole receiving array for estimating the position of a diver in shallow water using electromagnetic waves is investigated. Due to the effect of fluctuations in the received power distribution, the diver's area may be estimated to be in a different position than it should be. In our experiment, the diver’s position is uniquely determined in 88.7 % area units at a depth of 20 mm in our pseudo scale model.

articleTitle: Design of Wideband Dielectric Resonator Antenna for D-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a wideband dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is proposed for the D-band antenna-in-package (AiP) solution. A low-cost AiP solution based on the high density interconnect (HDI) printed circuit board (PCB) process is proposed for the first time for D-band applications. The radio-frequency (RF) chip is embedded in the multi-layer PCBs and packaged with flip-chip bonding. The RF signal is transferred from the chip to the top of the package by a vertical transition for antenna excitation. As an example, the DRA (0.5 mm Alumina cube) is designed with a single-ended microstrip-fed on the package top. The measured impedance matching bandwidth is 115-162 GHz with a peak gain of 5.5 dBi at 154 GHz.

articleTitle: A Switchable Linear to Circular Polarization Converter Using PIN Diodes
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we present a method to design a switchable polarizer using p-i-n diodes. An antenna-filter-antenna architecture with four metal layers (receiving and transmitting radiating elements, ground plane, and bias lines) is implemented to convert an impinging linearly-polarized electromagnetic wave to a circularly-polarized one. Furthermore, by controlling opportunely the bias current flowing on the two pi-n diodes flip chipped on the transmitting radiating element, the transmission wave can be switched to either left-handed circular polarization (LHCP) or right-handed circular polarization (RHCP). Full-wave electromagnetic simulations of a single element show a transmission loss < 0.8 dB for both polarization (LHCP/RHCP) and 180° phase difference in the frequency band (27 - 31 GHz).

articleTitle: Metal-only Reflecting Luneburg Lens Design for Sub-THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a metasurface (MTS) beam-former based on Reflecting Luneburg Lenses (RLLs) operating in the sub-THz range. RLLs consist of two circular parallel plate waveguides (PPWs) vertically stacked. The bottom wall of the lower PPW is loaded with a MTS with an axially symmetric modulation. The wave launched by a primary feed in the bottom PPW is collimated in the top one, so that a plane wave is identically generated for any azimuthal position of the source. The proposed solution uses a bed of nails, well-suited to fabrication by Si micromachining, to implement the RLL refractive index profile. Simulation results yield a 30% -3dB directivity bandwidth around the center frequency (280 GHz). This device can be used as a beam-former for multi-beam antennas for Earth observation or for front- and back-hauling in beyond 5G wireless.

articleTitle: An FDTD Analysis of a Sensing Technique Based on Variation of Reflection Characteristics of an Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper discusses detection of presence of a target near an antenna. In order to clarify the feasibility of the sensing technique, we analyzed the change of the frequency characteristics of the return loss in the presence or absence of the target object near the antenna. As the target object we assume human body and a sheet of paper. Numerical analysis using the FDTD method was performed. By the results, we confirmed detectable amount of change can be observed.

articleTitle: Band Enhancement of a Compact Flexible Antenna for WLAN, Wi-Fi and C-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Design and analysis of a wideband compact flexible antenna is presented in this paper. The bandwidth enhancement of conventional triangular quarter wave monopole antenna is achieved by utilizing the combination of a fractal structure along with open ended stub. Moreover, the flexibility analysis was studied to show the stability of presented work for conformal analysis. Furthermore, compact size, wideband, stable performance in flexibility condition makes the proposed work potential candidate for WLAN, Wi-Fi and C-band Applications.

articleTitle: Compact Multi-Input Multi-Output Loop Antenna System for 5G Laptops
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a compact configured 5G dual-band multi-input multi-output (MIMO) loop antenna system for laptop computers. The antenna system is consisted of two identical 95 × 2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> four-antenna units that are allocated on the top edge of the display ground plane and are 10 mm away from both the left and right sides. Each four-antenna unit is a two-dimensional loop antenna of the same structure and size. The loop antenna is composed of a T-shaped feed-in section and a double short-circuit loop. In addition, the four loop antennas are arranged in the same direction and side by side with only 1 mm space to form a high-isolation four-antenna unit. The two sets of four-antenna units can be used in 5G dual-bands of 3,300-3,600 MHz and 4,800-5,000 MHz. The measured isolation results between eight antennas were all better than 15 dB while the measured antenna efficiencies were between 35% and 65%, and the measured envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) calculated from the electric-field radiation pattern were all less than 0.2.

articleTitle: A 4×4 Planar Dual-Polarization Retrodirective Array
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The passive Retrodirective Array (RDA) can increase the RCS of the antenna array in a wide-angle range without excitation. In this work, we design a Planar Dual-polarization Retrodirective Array which has the polarization rotation function. Because more transmission lines are needed, the complexity of the RDA with polarization rotation function is twice that of the ordinary RDA. By designing the phase conjugation network with a multi-layer structure, we place 16 transmission lines of equal length in a small antenna aperture. The simulation results show that the RDA’s 3dB beamwidth of the Monostatic RCS is about ±40° which has a great improvement in the wide-angle range compared with the metal plane of the same size.

articleTitle: Design of Multifunctional Reflectarray Elements Based on the Switchable Ground Plane
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we proposed a novel multifunctional reflectarray (RA) element which consists of resistor layer, switchable ground plane (SGP) layer and ground layer. The SGP consists of a frequency selective surface (FSS) and four PIN diodes. By switching the status of diodes, the SGP operates as ground or transparency to the incident waves thus the distance between the resistor layer and the ground is changed accordingly, which makes the incident power reflected or absorbed by the proposed RA element. The principle is explained and the simulated results show that the reflection coefficient is - 0.18 dB for reflector status and - 20 dB for absorber status. Moreover, the dynamic control of the reflected amplitude can be easily realized by using resistors with different resistance. The additional control of the reflected amplitude makes RA antennas more flexible and powerful in realizing complicated beam-forming applications.

articleTitle: Semianalytically Designed, Transverse Magnetic, Printed Circuit Board Metagratings
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We propose a novel printed-circuit-board (PCB) compatible configuration for transverse magnetic (TM) polarized metagratings (MG), followed by a semianalytical design method. These sparse periodic arrangements of subwavelength polarizable particles are typically designed using detailed Floquet-Bloch-based analytical models, yielding fabricationready configurations exhibiting prescribed scattering patterns. To advance these models beyond single-polarized MGs demonstrated so far, we utilize dog-bone metallic elements to facilitate interaction with TM waves, and show that the canonical dipole line model can be used to analyze and synthesize such MGs. We demonstrate the efficacy of the proposed methodology by designing perfect MG beam splitters, verified via full-wave simulations. These results lay the grounds for complete semianalytical design of dual polarized PCB MGs.

articleTitle: Side-lobes Suppression for 5G Millimeter Wave Sparse Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In many 5G engineering applications, narrow scanning beams is required for antenna array without corresponding gain. This type of application can also be achieved by adopting a non-periodic arrangement of the antenna elements on the array aperture to reduce the cost of the antenna system by achieving technical specifications with fewer antenna elements and suppression of side lobes. Therefore, this paper is aimed at synthesizing different constraints for the millimeter wave non-periodic sparsely distributed antenna array. The genetic algorithm is applied to different constraints of non-periodic distributed arrays to optimize the array layout. In the sparse optimization problem of millimeter wave planar array, sometimes it is necessary to meet certain specific requirements. For example, in order to ensure a certain array aperture, array elements must be provided at the four corners of the planar array. In order to ensure the sum or the difference radiation pattern, the sparse plane array is required to be symmetrical on the top, the bottom, the left and the right.

articleTitle: Broadband Measurement of Dielectric Constant on FR-4 PCB by Using Discontinuous Microstrip Lines
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose to investigate the use of the equivalent mode for the discontinuous microstrip lines to measure the dielectric constant of the substrate within the high-frequency printed circuit boards. Our planar-circuit non-resonant method of this project is based on standard two-port transmission/reflection methods and can be used to determine the effective dielectric constant over broadband frequencies. A simplified measurement formula is obtained by self-calibration using two different structures of microstrip lines, which can avoid more complicated calculations. Comparing to the previous work, we use a more accurate equivalent model for the discontinuous microstrip lines and the effect of dispersion on high frequency-microstrip lines are also considered in this method. The trace functions can be calculated from the calculations of the measurement results, and the dielectric constants will then be determined. The experimental setup of this method is easy to be implemented and low cost. According to my understanding, the measurement results are more accurate comparing to other methods. This measurement method for the dielectric constant can be adopted and used in the high-frequency laboratory with vector network analyzers.

articleTitle: Coherent Phase Calibration of the 5G Massive MIMO Devices Using CATR OTA Test Method
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study proposes the modified element-excitation method (EEM) for the coherent phase calibration of the mm-wave active phased array antenna in CATR chamber. The experimental study of a 32-element mm-wave phased array antenna validates the proposed method.

articleTitle: Enhancing and Localizing Surface Wave Propagation with Reconfigurable Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: As an attempt to develop a reconfigurable surface architecture that can use liquid metal such as Galinstan to shape surface channels on demand, this paper considers a punctured surface where cavities are evenly distributed and can be filled with liquid metal potentially via digitally controlled pumps. In this paper, we look at the benefits of such architecture in terms of surface-wave signal enhancement and isolation, and examine how various system parameters impact the performance using full wave 3-dimensional electromagnetic simulations. It is shown that extraordinary signal shaping can be obtained.

articleTitle: Optimized High Gaussicity Smooth Spline-Profile Feed Horns for Terahertz Defog Camera
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of smooth spline-profile feed horns for a novel terahertz passive imaging application—a terahertz defog camera suitable for indoor fire environment monitoring. A method has been proposed which, for a particular desired imaging spatial resolution, can optimize the horn profile for good radiation symmetry and high Gaussicity. The simulated results achieve a Gaussian coupling efficiency exceeding 98%, a gain of 25.3 dBi, a -10 dB HPBW of 9.3°, peak cross-polarizations below -28 dB, and sidelobes at the -30 dB level at 94Ghz. Furthermore, the imaging performance of a focal-plane-array-fed terahertz defog camera is well tested, proving that a smooth-walled spline-profile horn is an easier-processing alternative to the corrugated horn for wideband terahertz millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: A microstrip patch antenna design based on ANN
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, an artificial neural network (ANN) model is proposed to predict the desired performance of a microstrip patch antenna which works at the center frequency at 10.2 GHz with a 1 GHz frequency bandwidth. In this model, a general methodology for the fitting of the calculated responses with rational function approximations was used in the description of S-parameter, gain, and directivity. In this case, the aforementioned performances of the antenna were replaced by the orders, residuals, and poles of the rational functions. A dataset of the correspondence between the geometrical variables of the microstrip patch antenna and the responses were collected in the state-of-the-art EM-CAD (Electromagnetic computer-aided design) software for training the ANN and further test. A validation was employed to confirm the validity and efficiency of this proposed method.

articleTitle: Measurement of Far Field Radiation Pattern of 300GHz-band Cassegrain Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We measured far field pattern of a 300-GHz Cassegrain antenna. The far-field measurement of the high-gain antenna requires a transmission distance of several tens of meters or more, and the receiver system requires a dynamic range of more than 70 dB and high sensitivity. In this paper, we obtained a 300-GHz-band experimental radio station license in Japan and measured the far field pattern of a Cassegrain antenna with a gain of 45 dBi. We also measured the near field pattern of the antenna, and calculated the far field pattern from the near field pattern. The measured far field pattern and the calculated far field pattern from the near field pattern are in good agreement. The far field pattern agrees with the antenna pattern models described in Recommendation ITU-R that covers below 86 GHz.

articleTitle: Design of Non-invasively Active Patch Antenna Integrated with Microwave Radiometer for Subcutaneous Temperature Measurement
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The paper aims at designing a radiometric thermometer for noninvasively measuring the internal body temperature. The radiometric thermometer consists of an active near-field probe and a radiometer designed in the 1.575 GHz band. The active probe integrated with a LNA is a circular patch antenna with short-pin loading and superstrate to collect the black body radiation under the superficial tissue. The Dicke radiometer was constructed and the probe antenna attached to a phantom was designed and implemented to test. The phantom based on Agar material was developed to emulate the real tissue of skin and muscle for experiments. The radiometer has a system gain of 50 dB, NF of 1.738 dB, 3 dB bandwidth of 90 MHz. The active probe has a noise figure of 1.1 dB and a gain of 13 dB at 1.575 GHz. The transferring rate of the power detector can achieve about 75 mv/dB. The measured DC voltage by the microwave radiometer is 2.676 V as attaching the cold saline water of 25 °C, while the voltage is 2.747 V as attaching to the hot water of 80 °C in the chamber.

articleTitle: Decoupling design of quadri-polarization overlay antenna element
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: OPRA (Orthogonal Polarization Reuse Antenna) can reduce the interference in the sector configuration. However, when a lot of antennas are installed horizontally, as in Massive-MIMO, the antenna size becomes large. In this paper, we present the mutual coupling reduction for a quadri-polarization overlay element. Overlay elements is the way to reduce the size of the antenna. The input characteristics and radiation pattern of the proposed antenna are investigated numerically.

articleTitle: A Thin Dual Slot Based Offset-Fed Beam Tilted mmWave 5G AiP Design
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a low profile antenna-in-package design for mmWave 5G applications. Aperture coupled feeding is incorporated with microstrip line exciting the rectangular patch radiator via two slots. The dual slots are utilized for enhancing the impedance bandwidth of antenna. A physical offset is introduced in the dual slots that is mainly done for obtaining a beam tilt towards the end-fire direction. Shorting via walls are introduced between the patch radiator and ground plane for obtaining a much higher beam tilt. Moreover, shorting vias also aid in impedance matching. The proposed antenna is wideband attaining operational bandwidth from 26 to 29.5 GHz that accounts for fractional bandwidth of 12.6%. Also, peak gain of around 7 dBi is obtained for the available aperture. Beam tilting is mainly achieved for directing radiation beam away from the broadside to end-fire direction since end-fire antennas are feasible and preferred for 5G mobile applications.

articleTitle: Effect of E-plane end shape on ripple suppression and focal arc of 300GHz band cylindrical lens
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A 4 sectoral horn E-plane phased array fed cylindrical lens was designed for 280GHz 28dBi E-plane fan beam. In simulation, mechanical H-plane scan across ±12° by sliding was satisfactory, but E-plane phased array scan was affected by 2.5dB ripple from standing waves within the lens. Modifying the E-plane ends of the lens by serrating or curving was found to suppress the ripple without affecting H-plane scan, but changed the focal arc.

articleTitle: Detecting Locations and Vital Signs of Multiple Humans With MIMO FMCW Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents methods to detect locations and vital signs of multiple humans with a multiple-input and multiple-output (MIMO) frequency-modulated continuous wave (FMCW) radar. Digital beamforming of virtual receiver arrays generated by the MIMO FMCW radar allows to find ranges and angles of multiple targets. Human targets are distinguished from stationary clutters by the proposed method, which estimates the lengths of their I/Q trajectories. These are proportional to the amount of phase variations. Vital signs of detected human targets can be also extracted through a phasetracking method using multiple frequencies of a FMCW signal. Experimental results show that ranges, angles, and vital signs of three human targets are simultaneously monitored with the proposed MIMO FMCW radar.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Aircraft Position Verification using AOA and TDOA for ADS-B
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: ADS-B (Automatic Dependent Surveillance— Broadcast) is an emerging means of aeronautical surveillance for air traffic control (ATC) where aircraft periodically report their positions to the ground. Although ADS-B can provide a better positional accuracy and update rate, anomaly position report has been concerned. Therefore, the reported positions should be verified at the ground before being provided to ATC applications. This paper proposes a position verification method combining angle-of-arrival (AOA) and time-difference-of-arrival (TDOA). The proposed method was evaluated by numerical simulations. As a result, reduction of miss detections was observed.

articleTitle: Multi-target Monitoring for Distinguishable Range Improvement Using a Hybrid FMCW-FSK 24 GHz Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an approach to improve the distinguishable range by using a hybrid frequency modulated continuous wave (FMCW) - frequency shift keying (FSK) of 24 GHz Radar. For traditional FMCW radar, the range resolution is inversely proportional to the bandwidth of radar. The proposed hybrid FMCW-FSK radar utilizes an overlapped chirp waveform. The distance corresponded to every frequency can be detected if the targets in the same range bin has different Doppler frequencies. Therefore, the fundamental theoretical limit of range resolution can be broken through applying the proposed waveform. From the experimental results, the distinguishable range is 27.2 cm for 150 MHz bandwidth, compared to traditional 1m resolution. Accordingly, the ratio of improvement is 3.6 times.

articleTitle: Compact Triple-Band Wearable Circular Patch Antenna for WLAN/WiMAX Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A miniaturized single-layer microstrip line-fed wearable textile circular patch antenna with triple-band characteristics suitable for wireless local area network (WLAN) and worldwide interoperability for microwave access (WiMAX) applications is proposed. By introducing an elliptical-shaped slot, a rectangular slot and a U-shaped slot to the circular patch with an all-ground structure, the antenna with a total size of 60×60×1.17mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> can operate in three distinct frequency bands, i.e. 2.41-2.49, 3.19-3.39 and 5.67-5.94 GHz, covering the 2.45/5.8 GHz WLAN band and a part of WiMAX IEEE 802.16 2005 WiMAX (3.3-3.4 GHz) frequency band. The proposed antenna shows good broadside radiation patterns, low SAR value and stable antenna gain in all of the three operating frequency bands. With the above attractive characteristics, the proposed design can be a promising candidate for body-centric communications.

articleTitle: Reflective Beamforming Metasurface Using Exact Incident Phase
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A method of using exact incident phase for the design of reflective beamforming metasurface is presented. Unlike conventional reflectarrays limited to point-source illumination or similar hence a stable phase center for simplified design, the proposed method addresses reflective beamforming with a more general (non-spherical-wave) source, from which the exact incident phase is used. For proof of concept, a reflective metasurface is designed to a non-spherical wave of convex wavefront. Beam steering at a specified angle is achieved by designing the composing unit cells of the metasurface. The proposed method paves the way for reflective beamforming with arbitrary primary sources.

articleTitle: High Isolation MIMO Antenna using Electromagnetic Band Gap - EBG Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the use of electromagnetic bandgap (EBG) structure in the MIMO application for mutual coupling reduction. The proposed antenna consists of a group of EBG structure between two antennas at different orientation of the antenna polarization. As a results, about 30 dB reduction of mutual coupling is obtained from the simulation process. This antenna is suitable to be used for MIMO and 5G application

articleTitle: Measurement and analysis of building entry loss in High base station environment
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: High-Altitude Platform Station (HAPS), which provides communication services from an altitude of 20 km via an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV), is attracting much attention as a new mobile communications platform for ultra-wide coverage areas and disaster-resilient networks. A HAPS can provide mobile communications services directly to smartphones. In order to design efficient cell configurations for HAPS-based services, we need a radio wave propagation model that takes into consideration factors such as terrain, vegetation, urban areas, suburban areas, and building entry loss. We measure and clarify the building entry loss characteristics at various elevation and azimuth angles environment. In this paper, based on measured results, we identified the key parameters required for the site-specific building entry loss model and proposed a site-specific model.

articleTitle: THz Photo-Polymeric Lens Antennas for Potential 6G Beamsteering Frontend
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a 3D-printed THz hemispherical lens antenna integrated with the open-ended rectangular waveguide at WR-10 band for antenna characteristics enhancement, e.g., gain and half-power beamwidth (HPBW). The digital light processing (DLP) technique, which is one of the famous 3D printing techniques, is chosen for fabricating the hemispherical lens antenna. The proposed design can be integrating the 3D-printed lens antenna without any extra assistant tools during assembly lens antenna with an open-ended WR-10 waveguide. In the simulation, the lens radiuses are investigated by varying from 2 mm to 5 mm in step with 1 mm. The optimum dimensions of the 3D-printed hemispherical lens antennas are obtained by using the 3D electromagnetic simulation tools. Based on the simulation results, at 90 GHz, the lens radiuses of 2 mm, 3 mm, 4 mm, 5 mm, and 6 mm, provide the maximum realized gain of 11.7 dBi, 13.1 dBi, 14.8 dBi, 15.8 dBi, and 16.3 dBi, respectively. The proposed technique gives many advantages, including ease of design, inexpensive material, low-cost fabrication process, rapid prototyping, etc. Moreover, the narrow HPBW and high gain of the proposed lens antenna can be applied to the 6G beamsteering frontend system.

articleTitle: A Double Band-Notched UWB Antenna Based on Complementary ERR-Defected Ground
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper we introduce the complementary electric ring resonator (C-ERR) for a defected ground structure (DGS) in deal with a double band-notched ultra-wideband (UWB) planar antenna. The microstrip-fed monopole circular patch configuration was used for a baseline UWB planar antenna. It shows the UWB band response over 2.513 GHz. With applying the C-ERR based DGS structure into the baseline antenna, the notched frequencies were generated over that of the UWB band. The mechanism of the coupling effect is potential to dominate the electromagnetic process between the C-ERR element and microstrip feed-line. The targeted notch frequencies were designed in a control of a relevant dimension of the C-ERR element.

articleTitle: 1-bit Unit-Cell For Ka-band Reconfigurable Transmitarrays
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a design of wideband unit-cell for 1-bit electronically beam-steering transmitarray antennas working at Ka band. The unit-cell needs two p-i-n diodes to obtain 1-bit phase resolution. The unit-cell structure is optimized using full-wave electromagnetic simulation. The results show that the unit-cell provides a wide –3 dB bandwidth, up to 26%.

articleTitle: Metamaterial Antenna Analysis using Wave Concept Iterative Process
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a Metamaterial-based bowtie antenna is proposed and designed for microwave applications. The Metamaterial antenna is modulated with numerical method WCIP: Wave Concept Iterative Process, to increase the simulation time and to ensure the speed. Because of its simplicity and precision, the WCIP approach has been seen as a very appealing approach to solving electromagnetic problems. This method shows a good agreement comparing to the Three Dimensional simulator ANSY-SHFSS with a minimum computing time, which proves the efficiency and accuracy of WCIP.

articleTitle: Linear Array of Leaf-Shaped Bowtie Slot Antenna Electromagnetically Fed by Microstrip Line
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a design of linear array of slot antenna operating within quasi millimeter wave frequency band is presented. In array structure, leaf-shaped bowtie slot antenna is used as radiating element. The array antenna is designed to operate within 27GHz to 29GHz. Each radiating element are electromagnetically connected to microstrip feeding circuit. Quarter-wavelength transformer is used to convert from antenna load impedance to 50Ω line. Throughout this paper, antenna characteristics are evaluated by using Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) method in commercial software (Sim4Life). Analytical results show that −10dB impedance bandwidth is within 27.27GHz to 28.94GHz which is about 1.67GHz. Actual gain has a peak value of 13.78dBi at 27.5GHz and −3dB gain bandwidth is within 27GHz to 29GHz.

articleTitle: Large Scale Characteristics of Millimeter-Wave Propagation Channels in Various Indoor Office Environments
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper reports the results of extensive radio propagation measurements in an office environment including four typical usage scenarios in the 58.32 GHz band. From the measured multi-dimensional power spectra, the large scale channel behaviors for delay time (DT) and azimuth angles of departure (AoD) and arrival (AoA) were characterized by the widely accepted large scale parameters (LSP) of path gain (PG), delay spread (DS), aimuthal spread of departure (ASD), and aimuthal spread of arrival (ASA). Those parameters were compared with those of existing 3GPP model.

articleTitle: Analysis of Pyramidal Horn Antenna for Ku Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper we present the design, simulation and measurement of a pyramidal horn antenna with linear polarization, operating in the Ku band at 13.3 GHz. The horn antenna is made of aluminium, weighs about 0.7 kg, the cutting of each face of the antenna was done with the help of a computer numerical control and then followed the assembly of each face of the antenna. The simulations performed with ANSYS HFSS show a maximum gain of 21.5 dB, which is in good agreement with the measured results. The pyramidal horn antenna proposed can be a very good candidate for telecommunication applications, atmospheric characterization, as the case of our project.

articleTitle: Improving Antenna Efficiency of Low-height-printed IFA Using SRR for Narrow-Bezel Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes an antenna design technique that uses split-ring resonators (SRRs) with lumped capacitors with the aim of enhancing antenna efficiency of a low-height inverted F-type antenna (IFA). SRR elements are arranged on the edge of the ground under the parallel arm of the IFA. Proposed SRR can be designed regardless of the size of bezels. By applying SRRs to an IFA, antenna efficiency is improved by 14.8 % at the operating frequency.

articleTitle: ISAR Image Inpainting Algorithm Based on DCGAN
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An ISAR image inpainting algorithm based on DCGAN was proposed to solve the problem that the image quality of ISAR imaging algorithm is reduced after interference. The proposed algorithm combines the theory of convolution and designs a network framework to complete ISAR image inpainting. The simulation results show that the peak signal to noise ratio and structural similarity index of the proposed algorithm are 28.51 and 0.90 respectively, which are higher than two other inpainting algorithms, and effectively improve the quality of ISAR images.

articleTitle: Parameter Study of Dual-Band Array Antenna for Stacked Differential Rectenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel concept of a dual-band array antenna to achieve large-scale stacked differential rectenna arrays. The proposed array antenna consists of three 2.45-GHz band and four 5.8-GHz band antenna elements on a double-layer substrate. The performance of the antenna is analyzed using electromagnetic simulation for the overlapping widths and element spacings of 2.45- and 5.8-GHz antenna elements. The antenna layout is optimized to have a high gain at 2.45 and 5.8 GHz. The gain of the array antenna is 12.2 dBi and 13.8 dBi at 2.45 and 5.8 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: Adaptation of Reflectarray Antenna to Yield Scanning-Spot Beam
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Herein, a novel reflectarray antenna design with a mirror configuration is proposed. Through adaptation of the reflectarray antenna's frequency and polarization (two of its characteristics that change beam direction), a multi-scanning beam can be realized, whose performance matches that of a conventional multi-spot beam with one reflecting mirror. A scanning-spot beam that changes beam direction using frequency in the elevation direction and polarization in the azimuth direction in the Ka band is examined. As a result, it is verified that the proposed design efficiently covers the desired service area.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of Compact Parabolic Reflector Antennas Using Partially Reflective Surfaces
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the gain enhancement of compact parabolic reflector antennas using partially reflective surfaces (PRS). The Cassegrain sub-reflector configuration is chosen as an initial antenna configuration. The physical length of the proposed antenna is four times shorter than that of a conventional center-fed parabolic reflector antenna while maintaining the high antenna gain by using a sub-reflector and a properly designed PRS. An example of antenna design with a dimension of 20×20×4 cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and the simulated antenna gain of 22.4 dBi is illustrated. It is found that the PRS structure properly modifies the electromagnetic field distribution of the antenna aperture to maintain a high antenna gain performance.

articleTitle: A Very Compact and High Efficient Rectenna for RF Energy Harvesting Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel compact rectenna operated for RF energy harvesting applications at 2.45GHz with high radio frequency to direct current (RF-to-DC) conversion efficiency is presented and investigated. The maximum conversion efficiency is 72.7% at 2.45GHz when the input RF power is 12dBm. And the rectenna can maintain high conversion efficiency in a wide input power range. When the input power is between -4dBm and 18dBm, the measured conversion efficiency can reach more than 30%. The Rectenna structure is simple and the size is compact, only 30mm×30mm×0.8mm.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Periodic Structures for RF Packaging of Integrated Array Module at sub-6GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Wideband PMC packaging solution fabricated by low cost 3D printing technology has been proposed as an alternative to conventional metal wall solution for isolating critical active circuits in integrated arrays operating at sub-6GHz. The two proposed periodic structures named as triangular pins and conical pins produce a parallel-plate stopband over the frequency range from 2.5-6GHz and 2.1-5.5GHz respectively. A test structure, containing passive microstrip lines placed on a FR4 substrate, has been used to verify the packaging performance of the proposed 3D printed structures and the measured isolation performance of the newly proposed periodic structures agree very well with the simulated performance. Isolation level better than 40-50dB has been demonstrated within the band of interest.

articleTitle: A Broadband Single-Layer Reflectarray Antenna Using Multiresonance Elements
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A linearly polarized X-band reflectarray (RA), based on single layer multiresonance elements, is proposed in this paper. To enhance the bandwidth, the unit cell is composed of double gapped square loops and a gapped circular annular ring. The pair of gaps are spatially orthogonal to one another, and two extra phase delay lines are attached to the outer ring. The unit cell exhibits a 600° linear phase tuning range by adjusting the length of the delay lines. A 277-element RA using a 15° offset fed horn was fabricated and measured. The measured results show a 1-dB gain bandwidth of 14.2%, and a 3-dB gain bandwidth of 26.4%. The antenna gain at 10 GHz is 25.2 dBi, which is equivalent to an aperture efficiency of 50.9%.

articleTitle: Printed MIMO antennas for 5G C-band for laptop computer applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposed a printed coupled feed antenna for laptop computers. The design of 8×8 MIMO antennas is placed on the top edge of the system ground of 200mm×260 mm×0.8mm. The size of the proposed antenna is 3mm×17mm×0.8mm. The antenna is printed on FR4 substrate of permittivity of 4.4 and thickness of 0.8 mm. The design extended to 8×8 MIMO antennas operating at WRC 5G (3.4– 3.6GHz). The simulated efficiency has a 47–59% over the operating band. This design with good radiation performances and keeping low profile is suitable for the application of laptop computers.

articleTitle: Study on Radar Cross-section Characteristics of Quadrocopter group flight
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, the method of moments (MoM, Method of Moments) has been used to calculate the electromagnetic characteristics of the quadcopter. The electromagnetic reflection characteristics of 4 sorties of multi-rotor aircraft in the air group flight situation have been carried out. It has been set that the frequency band is 433MHz that the incident wave magnitude is 1V/m and the polarization is a linearly polarized wave. The quadcopter was at a fixed distance of 3 meters and found under different observation angles (XY, XZ, YZ planes) that has been found that the electromagnetic reflection characteristics are peculiar. And under the convergence of simulation data, the near-field and far-field reflection fields have been discussed separately. The electromagnetic characteristics analysis of radar reflection cross-sectional area has been provided. Relevant data can be used as a reference for the formulation of flight plans when performing specific flight mission planning.

articleTitle: 79GHz Antenna Gain Enhancement by Using Planar Dielectric Lens on the Housing
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the gain enhancement of the 79GHz single patch antenna by using a rectangle planar dielectric lens on the housing. The dielectric lens is mounted on the housing and realized by a 3D printer. The lens consists of five different areas for phase compensation of electromagnetic waves. Different dielectric lens areas are manufactured with different drilling percentages to be equivalent to required effective dielectric constants. The peak gain of the rectangle planar dielectric lens with 17.5mmx15.68mm on the top of the single patch antenna is 11.9 dBi, which can increase by 4.75 dBi in the broadside direction compared with the standalone patch antenna without the rectangle planar dielectric lens on the housing.

articleTitle: Contoured Beamforming of Reflectarray Antennas for 5G Indoor Coverage at Sub-6 GHz Band
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Indoor radio coverage of mobile communication is relatively sophisticate to assure the transmission quality. A simple reflectarray antenna fed by a dual-polarized antenna is designed to produce contoured patterns at the sub-6 GHz band for 5G applications. The synthesis of the reflectarray elements decreases the transition region to reduce handover rate with relatively optimized field distribution. The design concept is presented with numerical examples to validate the feasibility of the antenna design.

articleTitle: A Robust, Flexible and Frequency Reconfigurable Antenna with Flexible Superstrate and Substrate
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a frequency reconfigurable circular patch antenna having dielectric superstrate to tune the operating frequency and increase the realized gain of the antenna. The antenna is designed with highly flexible, robust and inexpensive materials. The antenna is basically a circular microstrip patch antenna having a flexible superstrate, the antenna is designed in such a way that the height from the patch surface to the superstrate can be varied, which subsequently changes the resonance frequency of the antenna. This mechanical reconfigurable technique appears to be a simple and effective method of frequency tuning operation of a flexible antenna. Moreover, the utilization of the superstrate improves the gain and efficiency of the antenna. Numerical investigations of the design are demonstrated in this paper.

articleTitle: Design of 77 GHz Patch Array Antenna with Horn for Industrial Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a 77 GHz patch array antenna with horn for industrial radar applications. This kind of microstrip patch antenna achieves high gain, wide width and small beam angle in a small size. The results show that the antenna frequency band covers the frequency range of 76-81 GHz. It uses a non-contact measurement method, which is suitable for radar. It can use for liquid level of industrial storage tanks to measure in multiple tank environments.

articleTitle: Wide-Angle Scanning Dielectric Resonator Antennas for Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Phased array plays a very important role in modern mobile communication, and the wide-angle scanning ability of phased array antenna is important. In the paper, the wide-angle dielectric resonator array antenna is proposed. The proposed array antenna consists of a single-layer substrate and dielectric resonator. The 3 dB beamwidth at E-plane is about 150° and the beamwidth at H-plane is 100°. A 4*4 array antenna is investigated, and its operating bandwidth is from 24.5 GHz to 27.5 GHz. Meanwhile, the 4*4 array can obtain a wide-angle scanning from -60° to 60°.

articleTitle: A Substrate Integrated Waveguide Planar Slot Array Antenna with Low Sidelobe Level
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) slot array antenna with low sidelobe level (SLL) is proposed in this paper. The slot array contains a new method to make use of the internal mutual coupling between slots to achieve the desired current distribution with low SLL in the H-plane. In addition, to realize Dolph-Chebyshev distribution in the E-plane, a power divider is presented, including the design of SIWs with different widths, SIWs with corners bent in arcs, and T-junctions with two posts for the sake of achieving phase compensation, wide bandwidth, and high power-dividing ratio at the same time. By adding two extra posts to control the imaginary part of the impedance, a transition from conductor-backed coplanar waveguide (CBCPW) to SIW with tuning flexibility is applied to feed the antenna. The 64-element SIW slot array antenna is operated at 24 GHz with the simulation result of SLL around - 18.1 dB.

articleTitle: Research on Maritime Floating Buoys that can be Observed with Synthetic Aperture Radar Satellites
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the coastal fishery, it is becoming more important to measure the position of fishing gear such as set-net using SAR satellites. In this study, we studied the retroreflective structure using the Luneberg lens in order to detect the floating buoys such as fishing gear with the SAR satellite radar. A prototype of the Luneberg lens was made using 3D printers, and it was confirmed by electromagnetic field simulation analysis, and we analyzed that it has a focus on the interface with seawater and it has the property of retroreflective.

articleTitle: A Study on THz Reflection Imaging of Two Metal Wires Using Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper investigates the effectiveness of the compressed sensing algorithms: FISTA and HQR, used in synthetic aperture arrays for THz reflection imaging. Two copper wires were used as the targets which were placed near each other. As a result, FISTA and HQR achieved almost the same position estimation performance as MUSIC, and it was confirmed that both algorithms can also estimate the signal intensity of the reflected signals simultaneously in simulation. However, HQR is recommended for accuracy, and FISTA for simultaneity in actual measurement set ups.

articleTitle: Dual Band Horn Antenna Using Frequency Selective Surface Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The demand for high gain, multi band and reconfigurable type compact antennas are required for modern communication systems. In this paper, a unit cell design using U-shape with sequential rotations is presented to obtain dual passband frequency response. The unit cell design shows dual passband characteristics for the frequency range of 8-9.96 GHz and 11.53-14 GHz. In the complete high gain antenna design, 3x5 frequency selective surface array with X-band Horn antenna is demonstrated. The proposed reconfigurable frequency design has produced dual band impedance matching and a high gain of 13.09dB at 9.5GHz and 13.12dB at 12GHz, respectively. Most suitable applications for proposed antenna include communication systems requiring frequency selective, multi band and high gain antennas.

articleTitle: A Planar Direction-Finding Antenna with Reconfigurable Circuit for Scan Range Extension
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A direction-finding antenna that estimates an angle of arrival (AoA) in wide angles is proposed. The antenna contains four quasi-Yagi antennas and a beamforming circuit that includes phase shifters, power dividers, and SPDT switches. The SPDT switches reconfigure the number of elements to be excited. The simulation results verify the null steering range is enhanced as double as the antenna without the circuit.

articleTitle: Polarization and Beam Regulation of Electromagnetic Wave Based on Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The C-shaped split ring structure is applied in this paper to construct unit cells to convert linearly polarization signal into cross-polarization signal with high reflection efficiency. By reasonably designing phase-gradient between adjacent unit cells, the metasurface can realize beam control at 15 GHz. Simulation results have well confirmed that normally incident plane wave is reflected by 30° and 41°, which are in good agreement with the generalized Snell’s law.

articleTitle: Modified half-mode substrate integrated waveguide antenna design for 5G NR mmWave applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A modified Half-Mode Substrate Integrated Waveguide (HMSIW) antenna with dual-operating band, narrow beamwidth and high gain is proposed for 5G NR mmWave wearable device applications. The antenna with a compact size of 64.35 mm × 9.32 mm × 0.15 mm jointly with microstrip feeding and open load structure, by using PT150 substrate to operate at n258 (24.5 GHz to 27.5 GHz) and n261 (27.5 GHz~28.5 GHz) bands is presented. Based on suppressing surface wave and varied load effect, a traveling wave antenna with open load structure is introduced, highly directive beams at an arbitrary specified angle can be achieved, and the lowest sidelobe level is obtained. A prototype of the proposed antenna is experimentally studied.

articleTitle: A 55-105 GHz PIN Diode SPDT Switch
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A single pole double throw switch (SPDT) realised with PIN diodes and using a commercial process is presented. The switch is characterized between 55-112 GHz and achieves minimum insertion loss of 2.8 dB at 85.2 GHz.

articleTitle: A Series-Fed Patch Antenna Array for Biomedical Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a series-fed patch antenna array with substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) power dividing circuit is proposed to work in the 60 to 64 GHz band. It is aimed to support frequency-modulated continuous waveform (FMCW) radar operation for biomedical applications. Due to the required radar mounting scheme, the array antenna is configured with a 30°-tilted beam in the E-plane. The 4-by-5 array adopts a non-uniform patch width configuration so that to control the amount of radiation from individual patches. The proposed antenna yields a broad matching band up to 9 GHz and the peak realized gain is 14.4 dBi, which shall meet the biomedical radar need.

articleTitle: A Millimeter-Wave Bandpass Filter Based on Substrate Integrated Dielectric Resonator
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a substrate integrated dielectric resonator (SIDR) is utilized to realize a novel millimeter-wave bandpass filter (BPF) for the first time. The dielectric resonator is fabricated using substrate and packaged by multi-layer PCB technology. Two degenerated modes TEδ11 and TE11δ1 are used and excited by the slot coupling feeding mechanism. A prototype operating at 30 GHz is designed and simulated. The simulated result demonstrates a low insertion loss of 1.57 dB with a fractional bandwidth of 6% considering the metal and dielectric loss. Advantages of low profile, light weight, and convenience in integration can be also observed.

articleTitle: The Effects of Array Element Number on 28 GHz Propagation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: As 5G communication kicks off, millimeter wave (MMW) communication is also on the horizon. Current MMW communication focus is on the 28 GHz band, and the possible base station antenna will be an actively electronically scanned phased array (AESA). The radiation characteristics changes with array size, and cost scales with the array element number. In this article we compare the 28 GHz signal propagation characteristics in an area near Taipei 101 buildings with FEKO+WinProp, and compare the differences between a 4x4 array and an 8x8 array. The results seem to indicate the higher element number and higher gain of the 8x8 array does not make much difference in signal propagation loss map, multiple scattering from side lobs is the main factor determining area signal strength, and beam forming is vital.

articleTitle: A Wideband Millimeter-Wave Magneto-Electric Dipole Array with Pillbox-Distributed Network
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work presents a high-gain and wideband antenna array using pillbox-distributed network for millimeter-wave applications. The pillbox transition and the corporate feed network are combined together to provide equal-phase power distribution for all array elements. The non-uniform power divider is employed in the corporate feed network, which can suppress the side-lobe level in the E-plane of the proposed array. The magneto-electric dipole antenna is adopted as the antenna element of the array. The fabricated array achieves an impedance bandwidth of 21% with a maximum gain of 29.6 dBi.

articleTitle: 1-Bit Reconfigurable Huygens Element for Beam-Steering Transmitarrays
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a 1-bit electronically reconfigurable element based on a dual-layer Huygens resonance is developed for Ku-band beam-steering transmitarrays. The element consists of two antisymmetric metallic crosses printed on both sides of a dielectric substrate, which enables a non-reflection Huygens resonance. A 1-bit phase compensation is achieved by controlling two PIN diodes. For verification, the proposed element is fabricated and measured with waveguides. Good agreement is achieved between the experimental and simulated results.

articleTitle: Phase Parameter Extraction from UWB Radar Response for Non-destructive Inspection
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes phase parameter extraction from ultra-wideband (UWB) radar response and investigate the effectiveness of it for non-destructive inspection of concrete. The phase parameter introduced in this study contains information on the phase-shift of scattering by a corroded rebar and is effective for estimating the corrosion stage of the rebar. Simulation results indicate that the corrosion rate of the rebar can be estimated by using the extracted phase parameter even when the commonly used correlation coefficient is not effective.

articleTitle: Independent Dual-LP Reflectarray Unit Cell Based on Crossed Dipoles with Split Rings
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel reflectarray unit cell formed by a pair of crossed dipoles with split rings for dual- and circular-polarization applications based on [1] is presented. The structure provides not only independent control of the two orthogonal polarizations, but also a phase variation range over 360 degrees with acceptable loss (below 1 dB and 1.25 dB) in each polarization. An equivalent circuit is also provided along with the correspondence between circuit elements and the unit cell structure, providing physical insight into the reflection characteristic and facilitating the overall design process.

articleTitle: Design and Experimental Verification of an Ultra-Wideband Ridged TEM Horn Antenna for Partial Discharge Detection
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, an ultra-wideband (UWB) ridged TEM horn antenna is designed to detect the short electromagnetic pulse (EMP) emitted by partial discharge (PD) at a long distance. The antenna is simulated using CST MWS<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup>, and the frequency stability of its phase center is optimized. Finally, a ridged horn antenna that can receive nanosecond EMP signals with low distortion has been fabricated. Simulated and measured results show that the antenna has the characteristics of high gain (above 17 dBi), wide band (1-18 GHz) and stable phase center, which can be used for PD detection.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Radial Line Helical Phased Array with Antenna Elements Rotated by Motors
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel radial line planar phased array in which helical antenna elements are individually rotated by their respective connected micromotors to realize dynamic beam-scanning.
