We designed, fabricated, and evaluated a 7-circle array with 168 helical antennas fabricated using molded interconnect device technology. The prototype antenna exhibits dynamic and accurate beam-forming performance, and also exhibits a low reflection coefficient of less than −17 and high antenna efficiency of 77%.

articleTitle: Ultrawideband dual-layer Magnetoelectric Dipole with Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An ultrawideband (UWB) circular polarized (CP) antenna based on dual-layer magnetoelectric (ME) dipole is proposed. The final design contains a radiator with two layers in different structures, a pair of cross-placed Γ-shaped feeding probes, and a box-shaped reflector in a total size of 95mm (0.87λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>)×95mm (0.87λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>)×65mm (0.6λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>). Simulated results show that the antenna has an operating frequency band from 1-4.5GHz (127.3%) with a maximum voltage standing-wave ratio (VSWR) of 2.2. Superior antenna performance such as stable gain, symmetric radiation patterns, and high isolation between two ports are observed.

articleTitle: Simulation Results of a Foldable Reflectarray Composed of Four Triangular Notched Patches
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A foldable reflectarray antenna is proposed in this paper. The reflection element of the reflectarray is composed of four triangular elements to avoid a folding pattern. The reflection elements show that 330-degree phase tuning ability. An 18×18-element reflectarray antenna is designed and simulation shows 25.4-dBi directivity and −26.6-dB cross-polarization.

articleTitle: Recursive geolocation of unknown emitters using TDOAs of three GEOs
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper addresses the problem of geolocating the unknown emitters causing uplink interference on the geostationary satellite. One common method is to utilize Time difference of Arrival (TDOA) of three GEOs. However, this method has an inherent problem that the geolocation accuracy is not good enough due to fact that two TDOA lines are nearly parallel. Furthermore, there are misdetection of TDOAs when the interference signals are not received properly. In this paper, we propose a novel recursive leased square (RLS) based geolocation method, which improves the geolocation accuracy up to 14 % compared with the conventional method.

articleTitle: Study of Characteristic Impedance of Near-Field Antenna in Coupled State as Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: There are two ways of wireless power transfer by near-field resonance. One is CWPT (Capacitive Wireless Power Transfer) using electric field coupling between electrodes, and the other is IWPT (Inductive Wireless Power Transfer) using magnetic field coupling between coils. In both cases, the impedance of the antenna changes significantly depending on the distance between the antennas. As a result, it is known that the peak of the transmission efficiency splits into two peaks when the distance is very close and tightly coupled, and the transmission efficiency at the resonant frequency decreases. In this paper, a method to replace the coupling state between the antennas with an equivalent transmission line model is introduced, and explain the transmission efficiency by the change of characteristic impedance between the antennas. The maximum theoretical distance-dependent transmission efficiency is obtained by this model.

articleTitle: Ten-Element MIMO Array Using Stable Current Nulls for 5G smartphones
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A ten-element MIMO array comprised of four two-element building blocks and two gap-coupled loop antennas is proposed. The two-element building block exploited stable current nulls exhibits high isolation (>26 dB), which consists of two loop antennas. Without adopting any decoupling structures, the mutual coupling of the ten-element MIMO array is less than -14.4 dB, which is desirable for future smartphone applications.

articleTitle: Platform Excitation for Radiation Efficiency Enhancement Using Slot Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the platform excitation using the miniaturized slot antenna. The single slot antenna has a narrow bandwidth and low radiation efficiency due to its small size, however, the radiation efficiency enhancement can be realized by exciting the platform as a part of the radiator. The appropriate excitation position of the slot antenna on the platform is clarified by the characteristic mode analysis. The maximum radiation efficiency of 73 % with four slot antennas is achieved.

articleTitle: A Two-Antenna System for LTE MIMO Uses on Laptops with Metal Covers
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a two-antenna system to support LTE multiple-input multiple-output operation. The antenna appears in close slot configuration and is applicable to laptops with metal enclosures. The slot sizes are 3 × 280 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. It is placed on the half of the 310 × 200 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> ground plane. Two antennas are place on the two sides of slot. The two LTE slot antennas are excited by an π-shaped IFA structure of 27 × 3 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to cover eight LTE bands, which include LTE700/GSM850/900/1800/1900/ UMTS/LTE2300/2500). In order to reduce couplings among the two antennas sharing the slot structure, a capacitor and an inductor are inserted in the middle of the slot to improve the isolation performance. Improved isolation performances are observed in most operation bands.

articleTitle: A Compact Frequency-Selective Shielding Enclosure Design for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A new frequency-selective shielding enclosure is proposed in this paper. This enclosure design is for wireless systems to prevent the electromagnetic interference and to allow the total transmission of wireless signals. A prototype is realized to demonstrate the high transmission of in-band radiation from the internal antenna and the high shielding effectiveness to the unwanted out-band emissions.

articleTitle: Recent Achievements on Passive and Beam Steering Transmitarrays at Millimeter Waves
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper reports an overview of recent advancements on transmitarray antennas at CEA-Leti in collaboration with IETR. Two fixed-beam and an electronically-steerable prototypes are presented. The first fixed-beam transmitarray radiates orthogonal linear polarizations at K/Ka-band. The second achieves wideband high-gain performance at 300 GHz using low-cost vialess technology. The reconfigurable transmitarray leverages on an efficient and low-power solution to attain beam steering and switchable circular polarization at Ka-band. Excellent scanning capabilities in a field of view of ±60°, with low axial ratio are experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: UE selection method using determinant in Coordinated MU-MIMO
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a simple channel capacity estimation method using determinant of the propagation channel matrix is proposed. A transmission efficiency is evaluated when the proposed method is applied to the UE selection in Coordinated MU-MIMO. The channel capacity of the proposed method is larger than that of conventional method and almost equal to or better than that of SINR method.

articleTitle: Low-Profile and Broadband Dielectric Resonator Antenna By Using Air Regions
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A low profile dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with wide impedance bandwidth is proposed by introducing the air regions. This proposed DRA is fed by two symmetrical slots. The DRA modes can be excited and merged to broaden the impedance bandwidth by inserting air regions insider the DRA. This DRA can achieve impedance bandwidth of 45.8% covering the frequency band of 3.2-5.1GHz. At the same time, it has very low profile of about 0.07λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. A relatively stable gain is obtained around 6.25 dBi.

articleTitle: Radio Coverage Mapping for Cellular Networks in a High-rise Urban Area using Tuned 9999 Model
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This research aims to provide radio coverage mapping technique using an accurate propagation model and high-resolution digital terrain map. Radio propagation simulations were done using the 9999 model which provides steering parameters convenient for calibration. Measurement campaign was conducted in a high-rise urban area in Metro Manila. Lee Method was used on the actual measured data to smooth out short-term fading, but not eliminate the effects of long-term fading. Parameter tuning of the 9999 model was performed such that the simulation fits the received signal power obtained from the measurement campaign.

articleTitle: Wideband Phased Arrays with Large Scan Range and Low Profile
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Six designs of the wideband phased array antennas based on Wheeler’s concept of current sheet have been summarized in this paper. From the array structure point of view, the arrays with vertically placed PCBs and those with fully planar structures have been categorized. From the final goals, the efforts have been paid to the arrays toward larger bandwidth and those with as a low profile as possible. Photographs of the six designs have been given for reference in this each section.

articleTitle: Wideband MIMO Antenna with Decoupling Slots for 5G Smartphone Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna system operated at 3.3~5.5GHz band is presented for 5G smartphone. The eight-element MIMO antenna is constructed by eight loop antenna elements. Each loop antenna element is composed of a dipole with two branches. To increase the isolation between antenna elements, T-shaped slots are etched on the ground floor, and the isolation is better than 16 dB. Within 3.3~5.5GHz, the simulated efficiency is higher than 72%.

articleTitle: Design of Small Loop Antenna for Detection of Electromagnetic Earthquake Precursors
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the association of anomalous electromagnetic signals with seismic activities prior to an impending earthquake and proposes a possible system to detect such anomalies. The detection of such anomalies demands the design of a highly directional antenna. In this paper we have broadly discussed the design and construction of such antenna for receiving VLF signals. Using the antenna we have successfully received and recorded the background noises in a frequency band of 9.7 kHz.

articleTitle: Polarization-Tunable Phased Antenna Array Module at 28 GHz Band for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents an active antenna array module for base transceiver systems (BTSs) at millimeterwave (mmW) frequencies. The implementation considers the dynamic orientation changing of user terminals (UTs) to cause rapid radiation polarization variations. The BTS antenna array is thus equipped with a functionality of tunable polarization to comply with the UT antennas’ polarization for minimizing polarization mismatch. Antenna architecture and its characteristics of radiation polarization are presented with HFSS full-wave simulations and experimental measurements on an antenna prototype shown to validate the concepts.

articleTitle: Experimental Evaluation of a Wave Source Location Estimation Method Using UAVs
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, the pressure on frequency resources owing to the increase in wireless communication systems has become a problem. However, focusing on time and place, there are unused frequency resources, and studies are being conducted on the secondary use of these frequency resources. For secondary use, it is necessary to estimate the transmitted wave source position; however, it has not been possible in the past because of multipath and antenna size problems. In our previous study, we proposed a method using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) and clarified the effectiveness of the method by conducting simulations. In this study, we conducted experiments to simulate the proposed method and evaluate the estimation accuracy in an actual environment.

articleTitle: Automatic Deployment Planning of 300-GHz-Band Wireless Fronthaul Link in Metropolitan Areas
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In 6G mobile wireless fronthaul, it is planned that 300-GHz-band remote antenna units (RAUs) are mounted on traffic lights and street lights in order to achieve a short transmission distance with line-of-sight (LOS) environments. It is difficult to deploy a lot of THz wireless links with high density in metropolitan area with LOS environment and without inter-cell interference. This paper proposes an algorithm for automatic planning of 300-GHz-band wireless fronthaul link deployment. 87 RAUs were placed at the location of traffic lights/street lights read from the map at Shinjuku, Japan, and installed 46 RAUs on the rooftops of the buildings by automatic deployment algorithm in order to connect all RAUs to the center base station (BS) with LOS environment. We conducted radio wave propagation simulation, and simulation results showed that SNR and SINR of the automatically deployed 300-GHz-band wireless fronthaul links is below required standard demand of SNR for 100-Gbit/s data transmission.

articleTitle: Antenna Integrated with Dual-Differential Feeding for In-Band Full-Duplex Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An antenna having dual-differential and fully integrated feeding is presented. The multi-layer antenna consists of H-shaped slots, two stacked patches to improve bandwidth, and two differential power dividers connected within the system. Such an antenna can offer simple two-port feeding and high-isolation for each polarization state, making it useful for full-duplex communications. The antenna provides -10 dB impedance matching from about 2.2 to 2.5 GHz with isolation levels between its external ports in the range of 50 dB while the maximum realized gain is 7.8 dBi. The designed feeding arrangement does not require any additional cable connections or external couplers which are typically used in other dual-differential full-duplex systems. To the best knowledge of the authors, no similar multi-layer antenna configuration with integrated feeding has been reported previously.

articleTitle: Millimeter-Wave Conformal Antenna Array Concept for Metal-Covered 5G Mobile Handsets
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A mmWave conformal array with 1×4 slot antenna elements which is built on the rounded edge of the metal-covered mobile handset is proposed. To provide good beamforming performance using the conformal array, the phase compensation and side-lobe suppression techniques are employed. As a result, the proposed array offers 90° beam coverage satisfying 8 dBi gain for θ angles with 5 scanned beams.

articleTitle: FDTD Simulation of DC Plasma Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Plasma antenna relies on the conductivity of the plasma to convey microwave signals, however, designs vary between plasma antennas, and the best way to explore them is through simulation. In this article we simulate the properties of a 60 cm long DC plasma antenna containing in a 12 mm Pyrex glass tube using a commercial FDTD code. The Smith chart, coupling impedance, and the gain pattern are shown. We think DC plasma possess certain advantages over an AC generated plasma antenna like a more stable plasma column and easily adjustable plasma density.

articleTitle: A Novel Planar Perforated Hyperbolic Secant Lens Antenna for Milli-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel generalized hyperbolic secant (H-S) lens antenna is introduced using perforated dielectric. The simulation results show 24.7dBi of realized gain at 10 GHz with low sidelobe levels (less than -18dB) and 3-dB beamwidth of 9° can be achieved. The 3-D printing technique can be utilized to fabricate the perforated structure of proposed lens. Due to its intrinsic flat shape characteristic, this lens concept could be a potential alternative design for planar Luneburg and half Maxwell fish-eye lens for millimeter-wave application, avoiding using extremely complex conformal mapping methods.

articleTitle: What Can We Learn from Replicating Hertz’s Electromagnetic-Wave Experiment?
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Heinrich Hertz’s discovery of RF-band electromagnetic waves marked a milestone in electrical engineering. While we often attribute the origin of wireless technologies to Hertz’s experiment, his apparatus bore minimum resemblance to those familiar to us today. Connecting an induction coil to a dipole structure, he constructed a spark-gap discharger to generate and transmit pulsed oscillations. To detect them, he used a loop antenna and observed its induced sparks. Hertz’s discovery came in two phases. In 1887, he staged a setting to produce a signal pattern, which he believed to result from interference between electromagnetic waves propagating in air and along a wire. In 1888, he placed a metal plate opposite to the transmitter, and declared to obtain a standing-wave pattern due to transmitted waves and their reflections from the plate. Elsewhere one of us has shown and analyzed—through historical, experimental, and modeling studies—the crucial flaws in Hertz’s claimed discovery. In this paper, we further explore the pedagogical values of replicating Hertz’s experiment. At National Taiwan University, we rebuild Hertz’s spark-gap discharger and loop detector, and repeat his measuring procedures. To assist the measurements and unveil the physical characteristics of Hertz’s experimental system, we employ modern instruments such as an oscilloscope and a signal generator. We find that some parts of Hertz’s experiment or its modern variations have stable and clearly reproducible results. We can create a standing-wave pattern with his 1888 setup when the spark-gap discharger is replaced with a continuous-wave generator. We can also observe a standing-wave pattern, as he did, along a terminated wire with his 1887 setup, even when the energy source is a spark-gap discharger. Yet, some other parts—e.g., the standing-wave pattern with his 1888 setup using a spark-gap discharger—are difficult to replicate consistently. We believe that these different parts can serve as educational resources for different purposes. The more stable results can be demonstrated in class to instruct the basic principles of electromagnetic waves. The less stable results can be used in project-based teaching that provides opportunities for students to probe the complexity of a realistic experimental system, and to learn to cope with such a complexity.

articleTitle: A Dual Circularly Polarized Array Antenna for Ka-Band Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work presents a dual circularly polarized 8-by-8 array antenna using inbuilt polarizers for satellite communications. The design consists of five metal layers, including two feeding layers for the dual circular polarizations and a polarizer layer that utilizes a pair of sector cavities as phase delay elements for each sub-array. Two corporate feeding networks using folded E-plane and H-plane T-junctions are proposed to excite the radiating elements. Simulated results of the array antenna have shown that the axial ratios are less than 1 dB from 29 to 31 GHz for both polarizations. The realized gains for both polarizations are larger than 25 dBi at center frequency.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study of a Wide Coverage Dual-Polarized Phased Array Antenna at 10 GHz
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The paper studies the feasibility of designing and manufacturing a low-profile, dual-polarized wide-scan X-band (10 GHz) antenna array. In a large array environment, approximated as an infinitely large array, the antenna is capable of beam scanning up to ±75° with a bandwidth of 15% in terms of the active reflection coefficient (Γ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">act</inf>) below −10 dB.

articleTitle: IRS Aided OAM-MIMO Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The Capacity of Wireless orbital angular momentum-based multiple inputs multiple outputs (OAM-MIMO) can be improved by deploying Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) of a large number of reconfigurable passive elements to control wireless propagation environment. In this paper, we focus on IRS-assisted OAM-MIMO in multipath environment. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed system achieves a better performance compared to the conventional OAM based MIMO transmission.

articleTitle: Characterization of Ultra-Wideband Propagation for Liver-Implant Channel
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Ultra-wideband (UWB) technology has the potential to aid in the deployment of wireless medical implant for various novel applications. However, due to the severe impact of human tissues on electromagnetic wave propagation at such a high frequency range as UWB, the implant channel characteristics need to be carefully investigated for an efficient system design. This study assessed the liver-implant channel in time-domain for in-body wireless communications at UWB range. The UWB channel response is characterized for the 4.5-6.5 GHz band by means of numerical simulations with digital human model. Consequently, the very short root-mean-square (RMS) delay spread less than 1 ns is observed for the in-body communication scenario. The results showed the feasibility of fast data transmissions for in-body scenarios using UWB technology.

articleTitle: On the Resonant Electrical Length of Helical Antennas Placed between Metallic Parallel Plates
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Helical antennas placed between two infinite metallic parallel plates are investigated. This study is concerned with the resonant electrical length of helical antennas. The first resonance appears as the helical antenna is transiting the frequency gap between its well-known normal and axial modes of operation. A parametric study is conducted to calculate the resonant electrical length as a function of the helical parameters, namely the radius and pitch of the helix. The results are validated by comparing the solutions of two independent problems, one is driven with a source and the other is an eigenvalue problem with periodic boundary conditions. The presented results are useful in the design of gap waveguides where the periodic media are made of helical wires.

articleTitle: Design of 24 GHz Antenna Array for Powder Materials Flow Measurement Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This article proposes a pair of 1×4 antenna array in 24 GHz-24.25 GHz (ISM band) for transmitting and receiving. It has good isolation less than -30 dB in the operating frequency band. And the measured gain is as high as 8.9 dBi. The size is only 20 mm*20 mm. With Doppler radar module, it is used to sense the flow of powder, which can reach a measured distance of 1.5 m. The 1×4 antenna array be fed uses an equal power network. Rogers RO4003C glass fiber substrate is used for the milli-meter wave frequency band. It has a low dielectric constant of 3.55 and a low dielectric loss of 0.0027.

articleTitle: Indoor Radio Wave Coverage by Phased Arrays of Antennas at Millimeter Wave Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the investigations of indoor radio coverage by ray-tracing techniques. Multi-beam radiation patterns are employed in the numerical simulations. The signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) are employed as the parameter to justify the effectiveness of radio coverage. It is seen that the directional beams may provide higher gains, but may not provide a good coverage. A hybrid implementation of omnidirectional and directional radiations may provide a better coverage in terms of communication quality for UE system.

articleTitle: Investigation of NVNA-based IBFD Antenna Test using Spectrally-Overlapped Stimuli
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the novel nonlinear vector network analyzer (NVNA) setup for testing millimeter-wave antenna systems using spectrally-overlapped in-band full-duplex (IBFD) stimuli. Different from the commercial NVNAs, the experimental setup is established with user-defined digitally-modulated test stimuli and multisine phase reference, where two periodical test stimuli are designed with identical carrier frequency and the same tone spacing, and are simultaneously applied to simulate the realistic IBFD scenario. According to the experimental results, the components of received signals can be extracted for error vector magnitude (EVM) analysis from the NVNA raw measurements, which are the vector superposition of received and reflected contributions.

articleTitle: Chipless Radiofrequency Identification Using Pauli Matrix Decomposition in Unlicensed Bands
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An encoding scheme for chipless radiofrequency identification (RFID) is proposed to operate in the 5.8-GHz unlicensed band. Conventional frequency-coded chipless RFID requires broad bandwidths, which increases start-up costs and potential interferences with other communication systems. To develop a chipless RFID system that only uses unlicensed bands, the proposed system exploits four split-ring resonators (SRRs) with different polarizations as tags and two patch antennas for a reader. The backscattering signals received are cast into Pauli matrix decomposition, which enables polarization diversity and the enhancement of robustness. As a proof of concept, a prototyping system with 2 bits is developed at 5.8 GHz. The Pauli vectors obtained can detect the coded information correctly.

articleTitle: Multipath Tracking of On-Body Tag in Linear and Spin Motions
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we present the multipath tracking results of an on-body tag in linear and spin motions. We use an ultra-wideband (UWB) off-the-shelf Decawave kit for channel impulse response (CIR) acquisition, where a two-antenna anchor is fixed in space and a single-antenna tag is placed on a person’s chest. The multipath is extracted from the CIR at each snapshot by non-super-resolution CLEAN algorithm, and the extracted multipaths are tracked during the body movement. Two types of body motions are considered: translational linear movement and rotational spin movement. Both line-of-sight (LOS) and Non-LOS (NLOS) scenarios are incorporated. The results show that the multipaths’ track could well resemble the ground truth, and this observation is instructive for localizing on-body tag in NLOS scenarios with the assistance of, e.g., IMU.

articleTitle: Relationship between Local Peak SAR and MIMO Performance for 5G Sub-6GHz Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This study investigated the relationship between the local peak SAR and MIMO antenna performance in human vicinity at 5G sub-6GHz band. A 2-element printed inverted-F antenna at 3.7 GHz was designed to obtain the local peak SAR with various antenna to phantom separation distance, where their correlations with MIMO performance, such as averaged channel capacity and power imbalance of antenna elements, were analyzed using numerical approaches. The results show the feasibility of the method to estimate the local peak SAR using MIMO channel capacity.

articleTitle: An Excitation of Millimeter Leaky Wave Antenna by Through-hole Reflector and Waveguide Convertor
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an efficient method to excite a leaky wave antenna (LWA) at millimeter wave by using a through-hole reflector and a waveguide to dielectric waveguide conversion structure. In recent years, due to their high directivity and simple feeding structure, leaky wave antennas have attracted much attention in millimeter waves [1]. we present the through-hole parabolic reflector that can excite a leaky wave antenna in a single layer. We also propose the structure that can efficiently convert a waveguide to a dielectric waveguide, which is often used in millimeter-wave applications.

articleTitle: Adaptive Array Processing for Radar Measurements of Pulse Wave Propagation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Adaptive array processing techniques are investigated for their applicability to radar measurements of multiple body positions with displacements induced by propagating pulse waves. Unlike conventional settings for direction-of-arrival (DOA) estimation problems, body displacements arising from the pulse waves are modeled as having the same waveform with a certain time delay, which results in a signal correlation depending on the pulse wave velocity and waveform of the pulse. In measurements of pulse waves, we compare different adaptive array techniques in terms of their resolution and accuracy.

articleTitle: Thermal Enhanced modelling of 6-energy-level system
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We reported an enhanced numerical model with thermaliztion. The model is applied for the Finite-Difference Time-Domain (FDTD) simulation of electromagnetic interaction between light and gain medium with different ambient temperature, as well has sufficient computational efficiency. The algorithm is then used to study the lasing characteristics of a Distributed Bragg Reflector (DBR) laser with different temperature.

articleTitle: Research on an optimized structure of Terahertz Turbo encoding and decoding technology
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper mainly introduces the channel coding portion in the terahertz, THZ) communication system, and uses the CPU multi-core to perform parallel computing to achieve acceleration of the compiling code program for Turbo code. Optimized acceleration of Turbo code in four aspects, including reserved memory space, parallel cycle, and optimization of coding structure and decoding formula, thereby realizing shortening of code runtime. After experimental verification, the calculation of the compiling code time is performed on different code length data. It is found that the parallel calculation can be shortened by 56.6% when the input code length is 10000bits.

articleTitle: A Broadband 8-Antenna Array Design for 5G MIMO Smartphone Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An 8-antenna broadband MIMO array design for the fifth-generation (5G) smartphone application is proposed. The proposed antenna element has a small size of 33×5.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and it is composed of a feeding structure and a pair asymmetric grounded element. This proposed 8-antenna MIMO array can completely cover the 5G New Radio Band n77/n78 (3.3–4.2 GHz), and good isolation of better than 11 dB is realized between any two adjacent antenna elements across the bands of interest. The overall size of the 8-antenna design is 136×75×6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The detailed design method and results of the proposed antenna will be explicitly explained.

articleTitle: Design of Amplitude-Modulated Transponder with Liquid Metal
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a liquid-metal-based transponder for radar sensing applications. By taking the advantage of flexible deformation of liquid metal, the RCS of the transponder can be physically changed, leading to amplitude modulation. To increase the modulation speed, an array of 21 metal droplets are assembled and actuated simultaneously. The experimental results validate that the backscattering power is increased by 3.16 times when the transponder is actuated.

articleTitle: Modulation Recognition Algorithm of Radar Signal Based on ICanny-CNN
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Aiming at the low recognition rate on the composite signal modulation in low Signal to Noise Ratio (SNR), this paper proposes a modulation recognition algorithm based on ICanny-CNN. The simulation results show that the proposed algorithm can reach 90.83% at 0dB and 71.52% at -8dB. Therefore, the proposed algorithm has a good classification and anti-noise performance in radar signal modulation recognition and other fields.

articleTitle: Human Body Shielding Loss Model with Frequency Characteristics for HAPS Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: High-Altitude Platform Station (HAPS), which provides communications services from an altitude of 20 km via an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV), is attracting much attention as a new mobile communications platform for ultra-wide coverage areas and disaster-resilient networks. HAPS can provide mobile communications services directly to smartphones, but requires a propagation loss model of human shielding that can consider elevation angles in various environments. In this paper, we propose a propagation loss model of human body shielding with frequency characteristics in HAPS communications.

articleTitle: Multi-Tag Detection Using Multivariate Statistical Analysis for Frequency-Coded Chipless RFID
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a multivariate statistical scheme to detect multiple chipless radio-frequency identification (RFID) tags. This multivariate statistical technique integrates independent component analysis and time-frequency analysis as a systematic procedure. To demonstrate the proposed technique, we test the read reliability and compare with the direct approach that detects radar cross sections (RCS). The experimental results indicate that the multivariate statistical scheme leads to an improvement of tag recognition. In particular, when the separation between tags is narrow, the multivariate statistical technique enhances the reliability by more than 50%.

articleTitle: One-sided directional wideband slot array antenna for 28 GHz application
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the frequency bands used in 5G telecommunication, the 28 GHz band is drawing attention because it can transmit and receive a large amount of information. In this research, we designed a planar slot array antenna based on the one-sided directional slot antenna. In order to realize the wide band operation, the resonance frequency of each element is changed. We also fabricated and measured the 8-array slot antenna to improve the gain.

articleTitle: An Over 100 Gbps Large-Scale MIMO Antenna with Double-Helix Array
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a 256 × 256 large-scale MIMO antenna with double-helix array structure. The proposed structure enables resolving the difficulties encountered in previous studies via subarray arrangement in a three-dimensional configuration. The analytical results using the double-helix array structure reveal that it is possible to achieve a channel capacity exceeding 100 Gbps in a limited and small volume.

articleTitle: A Simple and Tunable Reflective Polarization Converter Based on Vanadium Oxide Built-in Metamaterial Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper a simple and tunable reflective polarization converter has been investigated numerically based on metamaterial which composes of a two-corner-cut square patch resonator embedded into Vanadium dioxide film (VO2) and reflective ground layer. All the results obtained by the CST Microwave Studio show that the polarization conversion ratio (PCR) above 90% is achieved from 1.46-2 THz at the temperature about 25 °C under the linearly polarized wave incidence normally. In addition, the influences on polarization conversion properties have been demonstrated with the insulator-to-metal phase transition of the Vanadium dioxide film (VO2) film by the method of varying the temperature. According to the results, the designed metamaterial could be applied in the area of temperature adjustable sensing, THz wireless communication, tunable polarized devices.

articleTitle: Analysis of Glide-Symmetric FSS Structures from a Circuit Model Standpoint
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the application of a rigorous equivalent circuit approach (ECA), based on a Floquet modal expansion, for the analysis of frequency selective surfaces (FSS) formed by periodic arrays of apertures stacked in a glide-symmetric configuration. Some numerical examples are explored, showing a good agreement with full-wave results.

articleTitle: Low-profile CTS Antenna with Circular Polarization for SatCom Applications in PCB Technology
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An ultra-low-profile, wide-band, continuous transverse stub (CTS) array targeting the K/Ka band is presented here. A pillbox coupler is used for the illumination of the array and to steer the antenna main beam in elevation by placing multiple horns in the focal plane of the pillbox coupler. The antenna is designed in multi-layer printed circuit board technology. The antenna presents a reflection coefficient better than -10 dB over a 48% relative bandwidth (19-31 GHz). A dualband polarization converter is added above the antenna to provide orthogonal circular polarizations in the down and up links in K/Ka band. Specifically, an axial ratio lower than 3 dB is obtained over 9.47% and 4.42% relative bandwidths in the two bands, respectively.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Analysis of Thin Film with Periodic Metal
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A thin film with a magnet-dielectric effect in Kretschmann configuration is investigated for evaluating an external magnetic field. The film is composed of gold and cobalt which are periodically arranged along the in-plane direction. Our investigation reveals the sensitivity of the external magnetic field using the periodic structure.

articleTitle: Simulation Design of Cavity-Backed Self-Phased Polarization-Reconfigurable Antenna Based on Liquid Metal
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a cavity-backed self-phased polarization-reconfigurable antenna based on liquid metal is proposed. The main radiator of the antenna is composed of two orthogonal dipoles. The surfaces of the dipoles’ arms are loaded with four microfluidic channels filled with movable liquid metal posts. By moving the liquid posts, the equivalent lengths of the dipoles can be altered, leading to changes in the self-phases of the two orthogonal dipoles. Thus, the polarization of the antenna can be adjusted. Moreover, this antenna employs a cavity-backed reflector, which can achieve unidirectional radiation. The simulated results achieved by CST Microwave Studio<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®</sup> indicate that the polarization of the antenna can be switched between linear and circular polarizations. The operating bandwidth of the antenna is from 0.72 to 0.77 GHz. The peak gain of the antenna can reach 10.6 dBi.

articleTitle: A Low-Profile Dual-band Circularly Polarized Cavity Antenna for Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a new dual-band cavity antenna that is circularly polarized and has high gain. This antenna is constructed by a novel dual-band asymmetric frequency-selective surface (FSS) and a 45-degree linearly-polarized dual-band patch antenna. A prototype for the C-band satellite communications is demonstrated. In the two impedance-matching bands, the antenna gains are higher than 9 dBic. In addition to the antenna performance, the shielding effectiveness (SE) of the added FSS acting as a shield is larger than 25 dB in the frequency range below 1 GHz.

articleTitle: Calibration Factor Pattern for Isotropy Simulation and Measurement of Three-Axis Electric Field Probes
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, calibration factor (CF) pattern is proposed for simulation and calibration of electric field (E-field) probes to obtain isotropy and CF simultaneously. Two E-field probes with different isotropy level, constructed of three-axis dipoles or patches, are simulated to illustrate how the CF pattern depict isotropy of the probes. By comparing simulation results of the two probes, it is suggested that the CF patterns could illustrate isotropy of the probes well, and CF could be obtained simultaneously. Moreover, the results reveal that isotropy of the E-field probe should be comprehensively investigated by measuring CF patterns on different planes especially when the E-field probes are of different configurations.

articleTitle: Spiral Choking Method for Scattering Suppression in 4G and 5G Base Station Antenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a novel distributed choking method, the spiral choke, is presented to address the cross-band scattering issue in dual-band antenna arrays. The operating mechanism of the spiral choke is analyzed, and its effectiveness in suppressing cross-band scattering is verified in a closely spaced 4G and 5G dual-band array. The experimental results demonstrate that the array with the spiral-choked LB element achieves mitigated cross-band scattering and has consistent radiation performance in both well-matched low and high bands.

articleTitle: Wideband Planar Microstrip Antenna Inspired by Metamaterial for Mid Band 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a wideband planar microstrip antenna with metamaterial unit cell at 3.5 GHz for mid band frequency 5G applications. The planar microstrip antenna is designed with square patch and two longitude slots at 3.5 GHz. The metamaterial unit cell is designed individually based on split ring resonator (left-handed metamaterial) SRR LHM type. Then both structures are integrated together. The metamaterial is placed on the ground plane of the planar antenna. That will increase the bandwidth accordingly. The proposed metamaterial antenna is simulated and optimized using CST software. A good return loss of greater than 10 dB and an impedance bandwidth of 1.04 GHz are obtained. This metamaterial antenna is a good candidate for mid band frequency for 5G applications.

articleTitle: Luneburg lenses for the new generation of communication systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Similar to reflectors, lenses can be used to increase the directivity of conventional antennas. The Luneburg lens is a convenient solution that permits multiple/steerable beams with no scan losses. This feature is desirable for antennas in both ground and satellite communications. Depending on the practical needs and physical constraints, Luneburg lenses can be implemented in three- and two-dimensional versions. In the case of three-dimensional lenses, the research has been recently focused in additive manufacturing, which can drastically reduce their cost of implementation. Differently, in two-dimensional versions, the research has been aimed at reducing the use of dielectrics, so losses are reduced, specially in the millimetre wave band. In this contribution, we discuss some relevant implementations of Luneburg lens antennas, and we summarize their use for communications systems.

articleTitle: A Circularly Polarized UHF RFID Tag Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a circularly polarized (CP) radio frequency identification (RFID) tag antenna design that operates in the ultra-high frequency (UHF) band. The proposed tag antenna has a size of 100×100 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, and it is composed of two main structures, namely, an eccentric circular slot patch and a coupled arc-shaped feeding strip. The RFID tag chip is embedded near one end of the feeding strip and it is also shorted to the main ground through a via hole. The size of the circular slot can aid in achieving good impedance matching between the tag antenna and the chip. The CP characteristic of the tag antenna is excited due to the feeding and slot position, as well as the gap slot loaded on the radiation surface of the patch. The 10-dB impedance bandwidth of the proposed tag antenna is 1.62% (914-929 MHz), and its corresponding 3-dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth is 0.97% (919-928 MHz).

articleTitle: Feed Antenna Optimization of W Band Active Millimeter Wave Imaging System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, with the rapid development of millimeter-wave technology, millimeter-wave imaging technology has been widely used in the security field. Active millimeter wave imaging uses the feed antenna to radiate electromagnetic wave to the measured target, and carries out image reconstruction according to the echo information, so the feed antenna plays a very important role in active millimeter wave imaging system. In this paper, a coaxial cavity horn antenna with a main lobe width greater than 100°, a relative bandwidth greater than 10%, and a heart-shaped pattern at 94GHz is designed. Then, on the basis of the horn antenna, the medium rod structure is added to reduce the main lobe width of the medium rod horn antenna to 23% and achieve the maximum gain of 18.7dB. It meets the requirements of the design indicators and the simultaneous imaging is better. It has theoretical guiding significance for the design of the feed antenna of the active millimeter-wave imaging system.

articleTitle: Accurate Reconstruction Algorithm of Millimeter Wave Holography
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Millimeter wave has penetration characteristics, which can make up for the deficiency of existing security inspection technology. Therefore, in recent years, millimeter wave holographic imaging technology for human security inspection needs to be researched and developed. In the process of security check, both scanning and imaging time and imaging resolution need to be taken into account. Therefore, it has great research significance to improve the imaging resolution of images and save the system costs. In this paper, the millimeter-wave reconstruction algorithm is studied, so this paper starts from the Angle spectrum theory in optics and deduces a more accurate reconstruction formula. This imaging algorithm makes up for the attenuation caused by distance, and 3D targets can get a more accurate reconstruction image.

articleTitle: Smith Chart Based Method for Rapid Design of Wideband and Multiband Quasi-Yagi Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, a design concept and a Smith-chart based graphical analysis approach are proposed to rapidly and effectively design the multiband and wideband quasi-Yagi antennas. In addition, a prototype of wideband antenna array for millimeter-wave 5G applications has been developed based on the proposed approach. The measurement shows that the proposed antenna array operates in 24 – 40 GHz (50 %) with a stable gain at approximately 10 dBi.

articleTitle: A State-Machine-Based Approach for Human Activity Classification Using MIMO Radar
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a state-machine-based human activity recognition method for an indoor monitoring multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) radar. Our method uses the transition of the Doppler radar-cross-section (RCS) in addition to the prior and posterior postures estimated by the radar to attain a high recognition rate. The experiment showed the proposed method achieves a 94.8% recognition rate on average.

articleTitle: Robust Beamforming for Antenna Arrays with Source Location Probability Density Function
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Adaptive beamforming increasingly finds application in new communication and remote sensing systems. In the beamforming, a weight vector is applied to the signals received by an array of antennas. The weight vector is usually computed to maximize the desired received signal and suppress interference and noise sources. However, the location of the desired signal source may vary or may only be known within a certain region. In such case it is beneficial if the beamforming can incorporate this uncertainty. Here, a new robust beamforming (RB) algorithm is presented and demonstrated which incorporates the location uncertainty through a probability density function for the location of the desired signal. The approach is demonstrated using an array of 10 patches at 2.4 GHz and four cases of the probability density function.

articleTitle: A Dual-polarized Electromagnetic Energy Harvesting Surface with A Simple Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a simple structured electromagnetic energy harvesting surface with a resonant frequency design at 2.45 GHz and a dual-polarization characteristic that can be used to absorb electromagnetic energy in space for applications in wireless power transfer systems (WPT). Unlike conventional designs, the proposed surface does not require complex combiners, but only uses channeling traces structure to transfer energy between adjacent surfaces, and is printed on a double-layer PCB with a profile height of only 0.0124 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>. This paper also further validates the possibility of multiple cell expansions that would allow the surface to be better adapted to low power density electromagnetic environments such as urban and semi-urban.

articleTitle: Frequency Reconfigurable Complementary Electric LC Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a frequency reconfigurable Metamaterial (MTM) antenna based on complementary electric-LC (CELC) resonator. The proposed antenna design consists of slot-loaded ELC on the ground plane as the main radiating element and excited by a microstrip line. By inserting two PIN diodes switches, it can switch to three frequency bands of operation. The antenna has been simulated using the CST Microwave Studio software tool. The simulation result shows that the proposed antenna is capable of reconfiguring up to three different frequencies which are 2.42 GHz, 2.56 GHz, and 2.70 GHz.

articleTitle: A Study on Location of Vehicle-mounted Antennas for Single-Frequency Full-Duplex Communication
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the location of vehicle-mounted antennas for the realization of single-frequency full duplex communication is investigated. Also, self-interference due to the coupling between the transmitting and receiving antennas is evaluated. Moreover, the appropriate vehicle antenna location is shown based on the electromagnetic field analysis.

Author Keywords: coupling between transmitting and receiving antennas

articleTitle: Design of Optimized Multiple-Frequency-Shaped Beam Reflectarray Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Previous research involved only optimizing the center frequency when designing a reflectarray antenna that radiates a shaped beam. In this study, we designed a shaped beam reflectarray antenna by optimizing the center frequency and multiple frequencies, in addition to using the conventional design method.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Enhancement of Printed Monopole Element Quasi-Yagi antenna using a Parasitic Resonator
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a method to enhance the bandwidth (BW) of a monopole element quasi-Yagi antenna (PQYA) is presented. A closely spaced U-shaped resonator (U-SR) with unequal arms in the end-fire direction is used to generate a new resonance at the high frequency. The evolution of the broadband parasitic U-SR is described. The prototype of the designed antenna is fabricated and tested with the size of 86 mm × 76 mm. The measured results show that the achieved BW is 1.55-2.67 GHz (53.1%) for |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| < -10 dB, and the gain is 4.05 ± 0.1 dBi for 91% of the BW. Measured and simulated results are in good agreement, which validates the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: Automatic Over-The-Air Evaluation of a Large-Scale MIMO Antenna Using a Switch Circuit
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an automatic method to evaluate a large-scale MIMO antenna in fading emulator using a switch circuit to measure the channel response of the antenna elements. In the proposed daisy chain MIMO antenna, the channel responses of the subarrays are obtained numerically with a personal computer by combining two antenna elements. Then, over-the-air (OTA) evaluations of the 64 × 64 daisy-chain MIMO antenna were performed, and it was verified that high-speed communication could be achieved regardless of the direction of the incident wave, demonstrating the efficacy of the automatic OTA evaluation method of the large-scale MIMO antenna using a switch circuit.

articleTitle: A Wideband Planar Array Antenna Using Both-Sided MIC and Leaf-Shaped Bowtie Slot Elements
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a 2×2 planar array antenna which is designed to operate over frequency band of 7GHz to 10GHz. Leaf-shaped bowtie slot antennas are used as radiating elements of the array structure. Both-sided microwave integrated circuit (MIC), which contributes to suppression of cross-polarization, is used as feeding circuit of the designed planar array antenna. Characteristics of the designed planar array antenna are evaluated by Finite Element Method (FEM) in commercial software (EMPro). From simulated results, −10dB impedance bandwidth is within 7.5GHz to 9.7GHz, which is 26% fractional bandwidth of frequency band 7GHz−10GHz. Cross-polarization level within half-power beamwidth in E-plane and H-plane are less than −34dB and −28dB, respectively. To validate simulated results, measurement of the designed array antenna characteristics is conducted.

articleTitle: A Filtering Antenna And Its Sub-Array Based On The Self-Shielded Coupling Feeding Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a three-dimensional stacked integrated filtering antenna, which is composed of four SIW cavities stacked vertically, and a rectangular slot is etched on the top of the last cavity to form a slot antenna. The antenna uses a self-shielded coupling feeding structure which can control the coupling more flexibly and make the antenna has a strong antijam ability. The filtering antenna was designed and simulated to be operated at 26 GHz with a bandwidth from 25.5 GHz to 26.5 GHz. It obtains an average gain of 4.5 dB, whereas a cross-polarization level maintains lower than 20 dB across the entire operating band. It also has a compact size 5.9 mm×4.6 mm×3.8 mm. Through a ball grid array, the antenna can be formed into a sub-array as a surface mounted component, so it can be applied to a 5G mm-Wave system.

articleTitle: Development of cable antenna for UHF-RFID identification
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, UHF- radio-frequency identification (RFID) systems are paid to attention as one of technologies which achieve the unattended shop or production field. These technologies promote the efficiency of inventory management and the spread of the unattended shop. However, it is thought that the execution of detailed inventory management with the long-range antenna is difficult. Therefore, the shelf antenna with the leakage cable which used the imperfect colinear dipole antenna is developed. In this report, results of evaluating the utility of the shelf antenna are described.

articleTitle: Multi-Beam Geodesic Lens Antenna with Enhanced Aggregate Gain in the Ka-band
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: New mobile generations, i.e. 5G and 6G, will operate in the millimeter-wave band to support higher data rates. Novel antenna technologies must be investigated to mitigate the higher losses in this frequency band. One promising technology for this specific application is geodesic lens antennas. Here, we propose an analytical model that calculates the far-field distribution of a geodesic lens. This model was used to design a multibeam 9-port geodesic lens with a widened radiation pattern. A coverage sector of 134° in the H-plane is achieved with a gain roll-off better than 3 dB at 28 GHz.

articleTitle: Compact Dual-Polarized 5GHz WiFi Stacked patch Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A 5 GHz WiFi stacked patch antenna array designed to connect bus shelters with high speed broadband is presented. A 45°/−45° orthogonal polarized 2x4 patch array stacked by 8 parasitic patches provides a 20% bandwidth (4.8 - 5.9 GHz), ensuring MIMO configuration with a gain of 7.8 dBi. Attention has been paid to the thickness of the antenna to ensure its discretion and its integration into the structure.

articleTitle: Measurement of Rice factor for In-Body Radios at 950 MHz in Indoor Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a preliminary investigation of the Rice factor (K-factor) for a medical in-body wireless channel at 950 MHz. A propagation measurement of the K-factor was conducted in an indoor environment by moving a cylinder phantom filled with salt water with a vertical dipole inside the phantom as transmitting side and an antenna mounted on the phantom surface as receiving side. It is revealed that the K-factor changes mainly due to the variations in the relative internal and external antenna positions, where the dependence on antenna types and polarization properties is relatively not remarkable.

articleTitle: Circularly Polarized Conical Radiation from a Metaspiral Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Circularly polarized (CP) conical radiation is formed using a metaspiral antenna made of c-type metaatoms. Electric current band theory predicts that the rotational sense of CP conical radiation will become left-handed at a low frequency of f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">N</inf> and right-handed at a high frequency of f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">H</inf>. The prediction is confirmed by simulation results obtained using an electromagnetic field solver based on the finite element method.

articleTitle: Substrate Integrated Waveguide Cavity slot Antenna at millimeter wave for 5G application
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper describes the design of an antenna based on Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW). The structure consists of slot antenna designed to operate at Ka band frequency. The effect of introducing slots and two feedline have been extensively studied. The basic structure is designed on a substrate with dielectric constant of 2.2 with a thickness of 0.508mm and loss tangent of 0.0009. The design consists of a SIW antenna fed with a normal microstrip to SIW transition. Multiple slots and different feedlines effects have been studied and analyzed using CST. Signal power reduces at mm wave frequencies as compared to lower frequency bands due to smaller effective aperture size of single element antenna. Therefore, in order to compensate these losses, the mm wave communication systems are required to have high gain antenna. A high gain and efficiency and low losses are major considerations which can be achieved by the proposed design. The proposed antenna geometry has a bandwidth of 1.27GHz with a gain of 8.9 dB at 26GHz and efficiency of 97%.

articleTitle: Propagation Delay Time Estimation in Street Cells by Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a propagation delay time estimation method by machine learning using structural parameters in a street cell environment is proposed. As a result of examination, it is shown that the radio waves with shorter delay and the small path loss, the higher estimation accuracy.

articleTitle: Miniaturized And Wideband Chipless RFID Tag Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presented the miniaturized and wideband chipless RFID tag. A compact and wideband egg-shaped monopole antenna with a slotted triangle-shaped ground plane tag antenna had been designed, simulated and fabricated with a dimension of 170 mm × 120 mm using PET substrate operating between 0.9 GHz and 2.9 GHz. The 0.17λ × 0.51λ omnidirectional monopole antenna improved the overall bandwidth and the gain antenna is compared to the conventional circular monopole antenna. The proposed egg-shaped monopole antenna can be integrated with the coding element as the transceiver of the transponder for the retransmission method that can be used for chipless RFID application.

articleTitle: A Study of Multiple Folding Array Antennas on Satellite Installation and Radiation Characteristics after Deployment
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A multiple folding array antenna that admits steps between panels, can furl and deploy using ordinary hinges and can realize two-dimensional deployment. In the deployed state, the steps should be compensated in phase to restore the antenna performance. However, the steps cannot be fully compensated out of the desired direction. In this paper, we study the antenna installation to a satellite and the radiation characteristics. It will be shown that the multiple folding array antenna is effective as an antenna for a small satellite.

articleTitle: Overview on glide-symmetric periodic structures
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this contribution, we summarize the special properties of glide-symmetric periodic structures. In particular, we discuss how glide symmetries can increase the equivalent refractive index and decrease the dispersion of two-dimensional (2-D) periodic structures. Also, we discuss how glide symmetries can be used to improve the isotropy of 2-D periodic structures, or alternatively, to increase their anisotropy. Finally, we explain how glide-symmetric structures can enhance the bandwidth and attenuation levels of electromagnetic bandgaps.

articleTitle: Linearly-Polarized and Circularly-Polarized Discrete Lenses for Wideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Wideband linearly-polarized (LP) and circularly-polarized (CP) discrete lenses are developed, based on the use of magneto-electric (ME) dipole elements. The wideband phase adjusting capability and stable polarization conversion property of the ME-dipole transmitting element are utilized and properly combined, to facilitate the design of such wideband lenses with desired polarization. The two developed designs that generate LP and CP radiations, respectively, both demonstrate a wide bandwidth of over 40%, which could be of interest for many wideband applications.

articleTitle: Phase-less hemispherical near field measurement using initial phase information by PR method
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The characteristics of an antenna are determined by the far field and several kinds of the near field to far field transformation have been proposed. The phase-less source reconstruction method is useful in high frequency bands, and we investigate the far field estimation using only the amplitude data on a single hemispherical surface. Based on the relationship between the amplitude and phase of the near field data, we propose to use the initial phase distributions in the Phase Retrieval (PR) method to reconstruct the source information. By introducing this relationship, the far field estimation can be achieved in high accuracy. This paper presents our proposed algorithm and verify it by the simulation and measurement.

Author Keywords: near field to far field estimation

articleTitle: Planar Sleeve Antenna with Choke Structure Composed of Zeroth-Order Resonator
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents the planar sleeve antenna with choke structure. The proposed antenna is designed with the planar sleeve antenna with choke structure composed of zeroth-order resonator. By using the zeroth-order resonator for the planar choke structure, the choke width and length of 0.12λ and 0.11λ, respectively. The relative bandwidth of 4.4% is achieved.

articleTitle: Recent Increase in Rain Attenuation Statistics of Ku-Band Satellite Communications Links
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The rain attenuation statistics obtained from Ku- band satellite signal for the recent 13 years after 2007 at Osaka, Japan, indicate the cumulative time percentages considerably exceeding the ITU-R predictions. These are caused by the increase in the horizontal reduction factor and the vertical adjustment factor of the ITU-R predictions. The increase in the vertical adjustment factor up to the ratio of 1.36 is found to be related to the average equivalent path length in each rainfall event, while the increase in horizontal reduction factor up to the ratio of 1.10 is related to the duration time of 5 dB attenuation. With these revisions of the factors, the ITU-R predictions show good agreement with the cumulative time percentages observed from 2007 to 2019.

articleTitle: A Unidirectional Ku-band Antenna With a High Front-to-Back ratio by Integration of Cylindrical DRA With Cylindrical SSPP Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a unidirectional pattern antenna with an enhanced front-to-back ratio (FBR). The resonator structure comprises a cylindrical DRA with a cylindrical SSPP and a reflector. Moreover, the proposed antenna with sidewalls attached to the reflector resonates at 12 GHz, i.e., in K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">u</inf>-band. It exhibits a gain of 10 dBi and a lower value of cross-polarization in the desired direction.

articleTitle: Optimization of a Metasurface Antenna Composed of Dual T-shaped Antenna Elements Based On Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In the antenna design process, traditional electromagnetic full-wave simulation requires too much time and computing resources. As an emerging technology, machine learning(ML) is applied in the field of antenna design, with good performance, and can solve the problems in the above-mentioned traditional methods. This paper proposes a metasurface antenna composed of dual T-shaped antenna elements, and uses deep learning methods to optimize its geometric parameters. The resonant frequency of the proposed antenna is 7.9GHz and 13GHz. The gain in the 13GHz can reach 16.58dBi .

articleTitle: Beam Switchable Antenna Array Design by Rotman Lens with SIW Feeding Lines for Vehicular Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, the substrate integrated waveguide is used to design the Rotman lens, and the multi-layer board technology is used to integrate the antenna array. Its operating frequency is set from 76GHz to 81GHz. Since the transmission loss of the operating frequency electromagnetic waves is more serious, the Rotman lens uses a dielectric waveguide design, and the antenna will adopt an array form to increase the gain and make up for the loss caused by the transmission path. This study uses a multilayer board to integrate the antenna array and the beam switchable circuit, which greatly reduces the size, and the three beams have a gain of nearly 18dBi in 0 and ±18 degrees separately.

articleTitle: A Novel CPW Wideband Circularly Polarized Antenna for 5G Millimeter-wave System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this communication, a novel coplanar waveguide (CPW) fed slot antenna with wideband circularly polarized characteristics is proposed for the 5G millimeter-wave system. In addition to the traditional inverted-L structure at front side, a pair of inverted-L strip and a parasitic patch at the back of the substrate are creatively added to the antenna. The simulation results show that an impedance bandwidth is 41.07% (22-33.5GHz), and an AR bandwidth is 20.1% (24.17-29.8GHz), covering the 5G band n257 and n258.

articleTitle: An Electrically Small Top-Loaded Monocone Antenna With Wide Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An electrically small top-loaded mono-cone antenna with wide bandwidth is proposed. By employing the mono-cone with top-hat, slot, shorting pins, cylinder, and sub-cylinder elements, the wide bandwidth is achieved. By connecting the shorting pins from the mono-cone top-hat to the ground plane, the antenna bandwidth at the low frequency limit is expanded. By employing the cylinder elements, the impedance matching at the mid and high frequency bands is improved. Furthermore, the sub-cylinder elements expand the antenna bandwidth at the high frequency limit. The -10 dB reflection coefficient bandwidth of the proposed antenna is ranging from 0.52 GHz to 2.12 GHz.

articleTitle: Wide-Multi-Narrowband Reconfigurable Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An elliptical monopole antenna integrated with slot dipole antenna with reconfigurable ability is presented. The antenna can switch its operating frequencies from wideband to triple-band to dual-band to single-band or vice versa by using switches. The operating frequencies of all modes are designed to operate within the wideband mode operating range, from 2.0 GHz to 6.0 GHz. Both ideal and real switches simulated results of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>, radiation pattern and realized gains are presented. By providing more frequency selectivity, the antenna is suitable to serve in multi-radio wireless applications.

articleTitle: A High Noise Immunity Monopulse Direction of Arrival Estimation Antenna for Vehicle Tracking
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, a new DOA (Direction-of-Arrival) estimation antenna for vehicle tracking is proposed to realize direct V2V (Vehicle-to-Vehicle) communications in platooning. The proposed DOA estimation antenna is based on the monopulse mechanism, and it consists of two microstrip antennas and a magic-T. To achieve high noise immunity, the sum radiation pattern has to be wider because the amplitude of the sum signal becomes low at large angles. The proposed DOA estimation antenna uses a high-permittivity substrate to increase the beam width of the sum signal. The high-permittivity substrate is also effective to miniaturize the antenna.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Radio Reception Environment in Consideration of Surrounding Terrain and Buildings for Temporal Disaster-Broadcasting
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Broadcast waves from temporal disaster-broadcasting are often transmitted from the rooftops of buildings such as local government offices. Surrounding terrain and buildings affect the reception environment easily since the broadcast waves are mainly received by car and portable tuners. In this study, we measured the received power of test broadcast wave of temporal disaster-broadcasting in the suburbs with undulating terrain and spreading residential area, and evaluated the effect on the surrounding terrain and buildings to the radio reception environment.

articleTitle: New Microwave Generator for 28 GHz band of 5G mobile communication using an Optical High-order Harmonic Generation for LiNbO3 Optical Intensity Modulator
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We have newly developed a microwave signal generator for the 28 GHz band of 5G mobile communication using an optical high-order harmonic microwave generation technique. Our developed generator consists of a DFB laser diode, a LiNbO3 Mach-Zehnder optical intensity modulator, a signal generator from 13 GHz to 15 GHz, and a photo diode. In the case of the input frequency range from 13 GHz to 15 GHz to the LiNbO3 intensity modulator, we can generate microwave signal from 26 GHz to 30 GHz with an output level of more than -6.3 dBm that is large than 13 dB from our previous generator.

articleTitle: Imaging of Object in Front of Human Body Phantom Using Leaky-Wave Focusing Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, millimeter-wave imaging using two rectangular waveguide leaky-wave focusing antennas in a quasi-monostatic arrangement was performed. One-dimensional detection of a conducting and dielectric cylinders positioned in front of a human body phantom representing the human body was performed by experiment to confirm the imaging capability of the proposed system. Two-dimensional imaging of a conducting cylinder positioned front of the phantom was finally performed.

articleTitle: A D-band H-plane Hard-Soft Horn Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Hard-Soft Electromagnetic bandgap material is a two-dimensional EBG material composed of a hard surface and a soft surface with an air gap between the two surfaces. A hard-soft EBG material for D-band applications is described. A D-band H-plane horn antenna using this EBG material is designed.

articleTitle: Design of a Miniaturized Annular Ring Metamaterial Microstrip Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A miniaturized annular ring microstrip antenna is designed by loading mushroom metamaterial structures. One annular ring antenna is numerically demonstrated using low dielectric constant materials with ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 2.2. It is observed to resonate at 2.546GHz. The effective circumference for the new annular ring antenna is 0.67λg. Note that this value is much smaller than the conventional ring antenna with a circumference of nearly λg.

articleTitle: A Flux Compensation Structure for Wirelessly Charging the Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A cross coupling (CC) structure consisting of a X-axial coil and a Y-axial coil is proposed in this paper for wirelessly charging electric vehicles (EVs) with compensations for the misalignments.
