The characteristics of this structure are then analyzed and supported by numerical studies reported herein.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost Partially Reflective Surface with Corner Reflector Antenna for Gain Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a metallic partially reflective surface (PRS) integrated with modified corner reflector antenna for size reduction while maintaining high-gain radiation. The 15-degree reflector fed by blended monopole probe is designed at 9.0 GHz. To improve the gain of the proposed antenna, the metallic PRS is properly designed and mounted on the top of the proposed antenna. The unit cell of the PRS is made from purely copper sheet to support high power application. The reflection parameters of the PRS (reflection magnitude and reflection phase) are investigated and optimized by using CST Microwave Studio. The gain of the proposed antenna without and with the metallic PRS are 5.5 dBi and 16.1 dBi, respectively. The proposed antenna also offers other advantages, such as ease of design, and low fabrication and material cost.

articleTitle: Realization of Broadband Butler Matrix-based Beamforming Network Using Reconfigurable Synthesized Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A broadband beam forming network (BFN) based on a 4-way Butler matrix is proposed to provide full beam steering capability. The key component in fulfilling the design is a broadband tunable power divider (TPD), whose power division ratio (PDR) can be theoretically tuned from –∞ to +∞ with a low reflection coefficient, and with good port to port isolation from 2.16 GHz to 2.64 GHz. The TPD is designed based on phase reconfigurable synthesized transmission lines (PRSTLs) as the tuning elements, in which the characteristic impedance is kept unaltered during phased tuning. In order to achieve continuous beam steering capability, two beam ports of the Butler matrix are excited with an appropriate weighting factor between signals, which is generated and controlled by the TPD. The average transmission loss of the feeding network is -3.5 dB and the average deviation of the progressive phase shift at the output ports is less than 20° from 2.16 GHz to 2.64 GHz.

articleTitle: QMSIW Cavities for Compact Dual-Frequency Millimeter-Wave 5G Antenna Array Design
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide (QMSIW) cavities for designing compact dual-frequency millimeter-wave antenna and array are presented. Two QMSIW cavities with unequal size are placed in a back-to-back manner and share a common row of vias. This leads to a compact dual-frequency structure. Each QMSIW can be designed and tuned independently. For demonstration, a QMSIW dual-frequency millimeter-wave antenna and its array at 28 GHz and 38 GHz bands for 5G applications are designed. Their simulated results are presented.

articleTitle: LTE-band Slot Antenna Design for Laptops with Metal Enclosure
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A slot antenna applicable for long-term evolution (LTE) uses is proposed. The antenna structure consists of two slots, one is an asymmetric T-shaped slot, which works in the LTE high band. The other is a L-shaped slot for LTE low band operation. The projected antenna platform is a laptop with metal enclosure. The openings of the two slot are placed on the metal rim to minimize visual intrusion. Several techniques are designed to meet LTE frequency needs. A feeding network is used to excite the two slots with multiple resonances. Parametric studies and simulations are executed to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed design in actual laptop environment. Result obtained suggests the design is suitable for LTE operation.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-Band Miniaturized Loop Antenna for Harmonic Radar Transponder
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual-band miniaturized loop antenna that can be applied to a bee-tracking harmonic radar transponder has been proposed. This antenna has the following characteristics. First, the overall size of the antenna is compact and measures 5 × 4 × 0.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Second, the operating bands of the antenna cover the fundamental frequency range between 9.3-9.5 GHz and the first harmonic frequency at 18.8 GHz. Third, the radiation patterns in both operational bands are similar and omnidirectional. Besides, a novel integrated matching circuit has been proposed to realize the impedance matching of this dual-band miniaturized loop antenna. The structure of this matching circuit is symmetrical without affecting the patterns and does not require additional SMD components. Finally, a prototype antenna with this novel matching circuit is designed and implemented.

articleTitle: Detection of buried targets under limited number of scans with a synthetic aperture radar
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Radar remote sensing of buried targets is widely conducted with ground penetrating radars (GPRs). Synthetic aperture radars (SAR) are widely used for monitoring of disaster, forest coverage, and infrastructure. For future utilization of airborne or spaceborne SAR monitoring of buried target, we investigated how to identify buried target for limited number of scans with using two-dimensional scanning GPR with synthetic aperture radar technique inside the room (GPR-SAR). Experiment of the radar imaging of multiple targets, buried and on the surface is conducted. Compared with 2-D and 1-D scans, it is possible to identified buried target adjacent to another target on the surface with 1-D scan as well as 2-D one.

articleTitle: Universal Complex for Sounding and Estimation of Ionospheric Radio Channels Ranging from 3 kHz to 1 MHz Wide
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Paper presents the findings of the research carried out with the use of the complex, developed on the basis of SDR, DSA, ML technologies, for active and passive sounding and estimation of HF channels ranging from 3 kHz to 1 MHz wide. Analysis of the sounding data of channels ranging from 3 to 24 kHz wide on a mid-latitude path of length of 2600 km showed that their availability decreases with an increase in the data transfer rate. At a radiation power of 100 W, round-the-clock operation of the communication system was ensured at the maximum data transfer rate of 1200 bps. It was experimentally proved that deconvolution compensates for polarization and intramode dispersion over the transmission bandwidth of up to 1 MHz. This bandwidth would provide an energy gain of up to 35 dB for fast frequency hopping signals. The gain can be spent to increase the channel capacity and reduce the radiated power, opening up new possibilities for HF use by a range of applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of an Interferometric AOA Antenna with Ground Plane in a Rician Fading Channel
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we conduct investigations on interferometric angle-of-arrival (AOA) estimation using an AOA antenna mounted on a ground plane in a Rice propagation environment. The results reveal that the proposed antenna can provide AOA estimate with high accuracy even in a Rice fading channel.

articleTitle: The Hybrid Over-the-Air (OTA) Test Method
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Massive MIMO devices require an OTA test to perform the coherent phase calibration and RF conformance test. To cover all test scenarios, the hybrid OTA test method is proposed and validated experimentally here.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of a Ka-Band Micro-Coaxial Collinear Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a super-miniaturized Ka-band coaxial collinear antenna is designed based on the micro-coaxial transmission line. The dimensions of the antenna are only 0.5mm*0.5mm*42mm. The operating frequency bandwidth is from 29.4GHz to 30.4GHz. The gain of the antenna is 8.40dBi, and the out-of-roundness is 0.04dB. The proposed antenna can be used for millimeter-wave mobile communications.

articleTitle: Gain Variation of Phased-Arrays with Normally Distributed Pointing Errors
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: When a phased array is placed on positioners, the limited accuracies of positioners would cause some random degradation of array gains. In this work, the array gains from an array with random rotations were evaluated and approximated by 2nd-order polynomials. Further, the probability density functions (PDF) were derived and agreed with simulations by the Monte Carlo method.

articleTitle: Design of exponential gradient TEM horn antenna for ground penetrating radar
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) technology is a kind of Ultra-wideband technology for underground targets. In this paper, an ultra-wideband transverse electromagnetic wave (TEM) horn antenna is designed. The size of this antenna is effectively reduced by adopting an exponentially graded horn structure, composite loading. Adding a metal reflector near the feeder further improves the antenna radiation directivity. The simulation results show that the designed antenna size is 0.50m×0.49m×0.33m (0.21×0.20×0.13λ). In the range of 0.125~3.1GHz, the voltage standing wave ratio is below 2, and the bandwidth ratio is 24.8:1. The gain is higher than 11.2dB above 1GHz.

articleTitle: Multimodal Transfer Matrix Method Applied to 3-D Periodic Structures
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, we discuss the application of the multimodal transfer matrix method (MMTMM) to compute the dispersion diagram of 3-D periodic structures. The problem of finding the complex wavenumber (both the phase and/or attenuation constants) of the different modes is posed as a standard linear eigenvalue problem in terms of the transfer matrix of the unit cell. The numerical drawbacks associated with the search of complex solutions in the complex plane are then avoided, thus making the MMTMM a useful tool to analyze and design periodic structures.

articleTitle: Vehicular MIMO Antenna Measurements in Outdoor Environments using Coherent Base Station Scanner with Real-time Demodulation
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An off-line coherent base station scanner has been proposed for evaluating vehicular MIMO antennas by utilizing the reference signal present in the downlink signal from the LTE base station. However, this system does not support TDD-LTE, and post-processing takes too long. This report introduces a coherent base station scanner capable of real-time FDD and TDD demodulation; it is verified it in outdoor environments. A prototype demonstrates good results which confirm the effectiveness of the proposal.

articleTitle: Low-SCS Microstrip Thinned Array
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A novel approach to simultaneously achieve low cost, low sidelobe level (SLL), and low scattering cross section (SCS) of a phased array is proposed in this paper, which is a combination method of thinned array and active cancellation techniques. A microstrip thinned linear array is constructed to validate the proposed approach. In the proposed thinned array, the passive elements are made use of and terminated by short circuits with optimized length to cancel out the backward scattering fields of active elements. Furthermore, the locations of passive elements are determined by a multiple dimensional discrete particle swarm optimization algorithm (PSO) to achieve a low SLL. Numerical study has proved the high radiation performance and low backward scattering characteristics of the proposed array.

articleTitle: Densely Arranged Array Antenna for High Output DC Power Rectenna Arrays
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper discusses the aperture efficiency of array antennas to achieve high output DC power rectenna arrays. Generally, mutual couplings between antenna elements with narrow spacing degrade each element’s gain. However, higher total output DC power is expected by increasing the number of antenna elements in the same physical area. The aperture efficiencies of 2- and 9-element array antennas are examined by simulation and experiment. It was found that the densely arranged array antenna improves the output DC power performance of the rectenna arrays.

articleTitle: Wideband Self-decoupled Dual Antennas for 5G MIMO Operation in Smartphone
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Two wideband self-decoupled dual antennas for the fifth-generation (5G) multiple-input, multiple-output (MIMO) operation in a smartphone are presented. The dual antennas are composed of a differential mode (DM) antenna and a common mode (CM) antenna. They are integrated into the same radiator for size reduction. Their feeding positions are arranged asymmetrically on the radiator, and the high isolation and low envelope correlation coefficients (ECCs) can be obtained without the need of an external decoupled structure. For the first example, the dual antennas are integrated into the rectangular radiator and have a size of 5 x 39 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> (about 0.05λ x 0.43λ) for operating at 5G n78 band (3.3-3.8 GHz). The dual antennas show an acceptable isolation of better than 12 dB and their ECC is much less than 0.05 in the operating frequency band. The second example follows the design rule of the first example. The dual antennas are integrated into the T-shaped radiator and show a high isolation of more than 20 dB in the 5G n77 band (3.3-4.2 GHz). Details of the two wideband self-decoupled dual antennas are presented and discussed.

articleTitle: Design of a Compact Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Flat-top Radiation Pattern
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The utilization of a transmitting antenna with flat-top radiation patterns is demanded in many applications. However, the existing antennas with flat-top radiation patterns usually have complex structures and bulky sizes. In this work, a new stacked rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is proposed to implement flat-top radiation patterns by combining TE<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">y</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">133</inf> and TE<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</sup><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">223</inf> modes of a rectangular DRA. The gain is improved by stacking a small DR with grooves. For validation, a flat-topped DRA operating at 5.8 GHz is designed. Stable flat-top patterns can be maintained from 5.78 GHz to 5.84 GHz. The 3-dB beamwidths are 87° and 58° in the φ = 0° and φ = 90° planes, respectively. And the relative sidelobe levels (SLLs) are lower than -13 dB in both planes. The comparison between the proposed antenna and relevant works implies that the compactness and simplicity in structure of the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: Design of Dual-band Slot Antenna Array for 5G Sub-6GHz CPE
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A dual-band slot antenna array operating in 5G sub-6GHz band with 8 × 8 multi-input multi-output (MIMO) is proposed. The impedance bandwidths through the operating bands can reach the 5G sub-6GHz bands bandwidth specification, respectively. The measured peak gains and antenna efficiencies can achieve to 2.5 / 3.0 dBi and 60 / 45 % in 3.5 / 4.9 GHz bands, respectively.

articleTitle: An Eight-port MIMO Antenna for Mobile Handsets
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, an eight-port MIMO antenna system for mobile handsets is proposed at 2.4 GHz. All the antennas are built from the frames of the handset, without adding any additional structure. The ground clearance is 2mm along all the peripheries. Among the eight antennas, four antennas rely on the higher order modes of the chassis to radiate, and the other four antennas are formed by the slots between the chassis and the frame. The isolation between the ports are above 10dB, and the envelope correlation coefficients are below 0.07 over the operating band, indicating good MIMO performances.

articleTitle: A Pattern Reconfigurable Antenna Design for 5G Communication System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a pattern reconfigurable antennas for 5G New Radio (NR) frequency band - N77 (3.3-3.8 GHz). The main radiating structure of the proposed antenna design is a modified swastika-shaped structure. Four parasitic arc-shaped elements are loaded around the radiator, and each parasitic arc-shaped element is loaded with a PIN diode switch for controlling the antenna radiation field pattern. By simply switching the four PIN diodes (D1 to D4) in a certain manner, multiple beam directions across the azimuth plane can be achieved, including the omni-directional pattern as well.

articleTitle: Estimation of 1090MHz Signal Types Used in Aircraft Surveillance System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The aircraft surveillance systems mainly use 1030/1090 MHz signals. 1030MHz is especially used for interrogation, and 1090MHz is applied to the reply and an aircraft collision avoidance system. These signals are shared with some surveillance systems. Therefore, as the number of aircraft increases, the number of signals increase as well. Managing the number of signals conducts the safety aircraft operation. Consequently, it is important how to estimate the number of signals. There are also some types of signals to obtain the information the air traffic controllers request, such as identification, altitude and so on. In this paper, we introduce the method using multilateration for estimating the number of 1090MHz signals. The result shows what kind of signals are used in present sky.

articleTitle: Tunable Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) based on LC Material for mmWave Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this research, we report a novel design of a tunable bandpass liquid crystal frequency selective surface resonating at Ka-band, which has a frequency tunability, closed to 5% of its center frequency. An LC-FSS prototype has fabricated by normal print circuit board (PCB) technology and a Merck-E7 LC material. The performance measurement has been conducted in a chamber through a pair of a transmitter and a receiver antenna. The measurement results have shown that a maximum frequency tunability close to 5% has been observed and the maximum frequency deviations were all less than 5%. These experimental results have verified the correctness of the numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Classification and opportunities of metasurfaces for antenna designs
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this contribution, we describe the operation of metasurfaces and their opportunities to produce innovative antenna solutions. Classical categorizations describe metasurfaces in terms of the operational frequencies, such as optics and microwaves. Another important categorization is based on the active or passive operation of metasurfaces. In this contribution, we make a classification based on their principle of operation. Specifically, we sort them out in four groups. First, there are metasurfaces that use Huygens’ principle to manipulate wave fronts. Second, some metasurfaces inhibit the propagation using electromagnetic bandgaps, which are used for example, to produce gap waveguide technology. Finally, there are metasurface antennas whose radiation properties are controlled with two-dimensional leaky-waves and two-dimensional lenses.

articleTitle: Lumped Reflection-type Phase-shifter for Sub-6 GHz application
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper investigates the bandwidth/phase extension for a reflection-type phase-shifter, which comprises a lumped 3 dB branch-line coupler and reflective load. A broadband 90° coupler is designed and compared to conventional narrowband lumped coupler. Furthermore, the impact on deviation of relative phase tunning range of the phase shifter applied by reflective loads is observed for sub-6 GHz application. Experimental result showed that the operating bandwidth of the reflection-type phase shifter is maintained while the relative deviation of phase variation can be lower than +/- 10° at desired frequency band.

articleTitle: Conductive and Dielectric Fully-Integrated 3D Printed Dual-Band Millimeter-Wave Fresnel Zone Plate Lens
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This conference paper presents a dual-band aperture-shared Fresnel zone plate (FZP)-based lens antenna for the V-band and D-band applications using conductive and dielectric fully-integrated 3D printing. In contrast to traditional full metal-based structures, double-screen grid structures are used to implement the concentric opaque rings of the FZP. Since the grids provide different transmission/reflection features at dual-band, they will not influence each other. A dielectric ring is directly printed atop the FZP for compensating for the phase-shifting from the grids. An antenna prototype is fabricated and measured. The radiation performance agrees well. The peak gains achieved are 20.3 dBi for the V-band and 21.9 dBi for the D-band, respectively.

articleTitle: A High-Gain and Wideband Circularly-Polarized Horn-like Antenna for Low Orbit Satellite Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A new horn-like antenna having high-gain and circularly-polarized characteristics is proposed. This antenna consists of four planar Vivaldi antennas and a one-port feeding circuit using a power divider and two couplers. For demonstration, an antenna prototype is realized to yield an impedance-matching bandwidth covering the entire Ku-band and a stable gain well above 12 dBic. Both the simulated and measured results show the stated performance.

articleTitle: An Experimental Study on Half-Shaped Printed UWB Monopole Antenna with Short Stub
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, an experimental study for miniaturization of a broadband printed monopole antenna corresponding to the frequency band of Ultra-wideband (UWB) system is described. This antenna has a half-shaped structure of a bell-shaped UWB monopole antenna with a short stub formed on a dielectric substrate (FR-4) and has a compact size of 30 × 13 × 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The fabricated antenna is possible to operate with the impedance bandwidth of 3.1 GHz to 10.6 GHz. The proposed antenna acquired broadband characteristic covering UWB band by measurement.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Channel Capacity Characteristics for Asymmetric LoS-MIMO
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, microwave and millimeter-wave bands have been considered for outdoor applications to cope with an increase in the communication traffic; however, the higher the frequency, the larger is the propagation loss. In this regard, a system that uses UAVs (drones) as relay stations to communicate in a line-of-sight (LoS) environment has been studied. In the system, there is a difference in the number of transmitting and receiving antenna elements between the base station and the drone and between the drone and the terminal. In this study, we evaluated the performance of asymmetric LoS-MIMO with a difference in the number of antenna elements between transmission and reception. The effectiveness of asymmetric LoS-MIMO was demonstrated by comparing the channel capacity pertaining to the distance between the transmitter and receiver based on the conventional symmetric LoS-MIMO with an equal number of antenna elements.

articleTitle: Researches on Frequency-Reconfigurable Metasurface Antennas Based on VO2 Films
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Vanadium dioxide (VO2), as a phase change material (PCM), is an insulator at room temperature but can turn into a high-conductivity metallic state when it is excited. Comparing with other controllable devices, it cannot only function from DC to terahertz frequency band, but also manage to achieve low insertion loss, high isolation and nanosecond switching speed. Three examples of VO2-based frequency reconfigurable metasurface antennas are proposed and studied. By integrating VO2 with metasurface cells, the antennas can achieve a large frequency ratio up to 1:1.61 and maintain high gain. In order to switch the operating mode of VO2 easily, a coplanar DC bias circuit with little effect on radiation performance is designed. The feeding parts of three antennas are all taken stepped waveguides with ridges through slots. These proposed VO2-based antennas would be potentially applied in millimeter-wave wireless systems in near future

articleTitle: Low-Cost AiP Array Design Using Machine Learning for mmWave Mobile Systems
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Based on low-cost PCB solution, an array antenna in packaging (AiP) dedicated for mmWave mobile systems is designed using machine learning. The proposed antenna operates at 28 GHz (26.5 - 29.5 GHz) with a gain ranging from 8 dB to 15 dB in the operating bandwidth. The development process of the proposed AiP is assisted by machine learning for prediction of the optimal radiating patch’s length and width in terms of resonance frequency.

articleTitle: A Filtering Hemispherical Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A filtering hemisphere dielectric resonator (DR) antenna (DRA) is presented. It consists of a conventional hemisphere DR, a ladder-like feeding line, and three slots etched in the ground. In this antenna, three modes, which are the fundamental TE111 DR mode and two slot modes are excited simultaneously. By making use of the mode-cancelling effect, two independently tunable radiation nulls are obtained beside the passband, producing filtering responses. Simulated results show that our antenna has a -10-dB impedance bandwidth of 17.4%, a gain of ~5.7 dBi, and a suppression level of 19 dB.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Channel Parameter Estimation for Indoor Environment Utilizing Reflected Rays Information
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years the discovery and utilization of the next generation of mobile communication particularly the millimeter-wave band has raised the demand to develop more accurate channel models. Due to the high interactive nature of the millimeter waves, accurate models which takes into consideration the effects of the objects in the propagation environments is needed. This paper presents a development of a machine learning (ML) algorithm for channel parameter estimation with the spatial propagation environment features. Objects in the environment are the main scatters for the radio waves, by utilization of machine Learning, a dynamic channel parameter predictive model can be realized. The input parameters to the machine learning prediction model are transmitter and receiver coordinates, and the reflected ray information such as the delay, angle of arrival, angle of departure, elevation angle of arrival, elevation angle of departure, and power. The proposed ML algorithm is based on random forest regression model. Ray tracing simulation is performed to simulate the channel propagation environment and statistical parameters are calculated by stochastic means to generate the channel impulse responses. Dataset used for training and testing the model are generated from ray tracing simulation.

articleTitle: LTCC End-Fire Array Antenna with Dual-Band and Dual-Polarization for Mobile
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Antenna substrate for Mobile needs to support dual-band and have dual polarization property and requires low height for 5G millimeter wave. In this study, we designed a thin antenna substrate with broad band and dual polarization property in the 28 and 39GHz band. The antenna utilized LTCC material (Dielectric constant 5.8, Dielectric loss 0.002@28GHz) was developed for high frequencies such as millimeter wave. Each polarization antenna was designed by log-periodic antenna, which is an End-Fire type antenna that radiates from the side wall of a substrate. These antenna elements were miniaturized by higher dielectric constant of LTCC material. From the results of simulation, it was confirmed that each polarization antenna for 5G application made by LTCC had broadband property. After that, the array antennas were designed based on these antennas (each 4 antennas). From this investigation, size of array antenna could be small (21.9 x 6.8 x t2.2mm). From the result of simulation, it was confirmed that array antenna could be operated dual-band and dual polarization. Next step is to product frontend module, which included the developed antenna and RF components (e.g. PA, LNA, Shifter, Mixer …), and will evaluate 5G application capability of this frontend module.

articleTitle: Switch-based Self-injection-locked Radar with Data Fusion Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this study, we develop a switch-based SIL radar system for non-contact human vital-sign detection. Radar signals from multiple independent antennas in the back of a person are fused to expand the effective measurement area and mitigate body position effects. The system is low-cost, requiring only a single radar with multiple simple panel antennas instead of multiple radars with specialized body-coupled antennas. Experimental and simulation results show that the proposed system can provide excellent results under various body positions.

articleTitle: Multiband Antenna for Multi-source Ambient RF Energy Harvesting System
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, we introduced a small size, multiband antenna for an ambient RF energy harvesting system. The antenna operates in most of the available frequencies in the environment, namely GSM900, GSM1800, UMTS2100 and LTE2600. The antenna is formed by an inner and an outer ring, each corresponds to two resonance frequencies. By analyzing the electric field distribution on the antenna and locating the right parameters for tuning, desired operating frequencies are obtained. With an omnidirectional radiation pattern, high efficiency and multiband coverage, the proposed antenna is suitable for ambient RF energy harvesting system.

articleTitle: Broadband Vortex Beam Generation Using a Pancharatnam-Berry Metasurface
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this work, based on Pancharatnam–Berry (PB) phase theory a metasurface is designed for generating broadband vortex beams. In this way, the transformation from incident plane waves to vortex beams carrying orbital angular momentum is realized. The structure proposed in this paper has the advantages of high purity, easy integration, and wide bandwidth. The working bandwidth of the unit ranges from 9.8 GHz to 21.3 GHz, and the polarization conversion rate within the working bandwidth is over 94%.

articleTitle: One-Port Near-field Antenna Measurement Using a Small Wire Scatterer
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A one-port near-field antenna measurement technique with a small wire scatterer is proposed. In the proposed technique, a wire scatterer is scanned with an interval of less than a quarter wavelength, and the measurement is performed at the port of the antenna under test (AUT). A two-dimensional phase unwrapping method is used to remove 180° phase uncertainty. The data obtained in the near-field were transformed to the far-field pattern. The proposed measurement technique was validated by measuring the near-field of an AUT over a planar scanning surface. The far-field radiation pattern obtained using the proposed technique was compared with that obtained from a conventional commercial anechoic chamber. It was observed that they agreed well, especially in the region near the center.

articleTitle: On the use of a Microstrip Antenna for Moisture Content Evaluation of Pharmaceutical Tablets
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Correct moisture content determination is crucial for the manufacture of pharmaceutical tablets. Microwave method is suggested in various literatures to be a promising technique for moisture sensing of various materials and goods as the microwave measuring technique provides an accurate and reliable moisture content measurement. Among different antenna types, microstrip patch antenna is widely utilized for the moisture content determination because of its inexpensive and ease of fabrication. This paper studied the possibility of using a microstrip patch antenna for moisture content evaluation in pharmaceutical tablet. To this aim, the microstrip patch antenna was designed as a sensing element to operate at the resonant frequency of 2.45 GHz. Consequently, the proposed antenna was tested with a pharmaceutical tablet model via the method of simulations. The antenna reflection coefficient was collected and used to estimate the different moisture contents in the tablet model. The results showed that the variation of the reflection coefficient is correlated with the moisture content presented in the tablet model which suggested the viability of using this microwave sensing technique as an inexpensive method for moisture content evaluation in pharmaceutical tablets.

articleTitle: Single-Layer Wide-band 45 Degree Phase Shifter with Filter Function
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a single-layer wide-band phase shifter is proposed, achieving 45 degree phase shift from 1.6GHz to 4.16GHz, and meanwhile exhibiting a band pass filter response. The proposed phase shifter is composed of a stub-loaded transmission line (SLTLs) with a delay line and an Open-circuited three-line MMR (OPTLMMR), both providing filter function. Constant phase shift is obtained by adjusting the phase slopes of main path and reference path.

articleTitle: A High Gain Broadband Circularly Polarized Antenna with Sector Dipole
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A sector dipole circularly polarized antenna is proposed in this paper. The antenna is fed by a semi-rigid coaxial line and the antenna structure is fed by multiple sections of microstrip line of unequal width and λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf>/4 length. The structure achieves four equal divisions of power and four 90° degrees of phase differences. For the array element, the conventional rectangular dipole is modified to a sector dipole, while the sector dipole is slotted for better matching. The improved sector dipole structure effectively extends the bandwidth of the antenna. The simulation results show that the impedance bandwidth of the antenna is 64.9% (1.55GHz-3.04GHz), the 3-dB axial ratio bandwidth is about 32.9% (1.70GHz-2.37GHz), the gain is 6.44dBic-7.52dBic, and the antenna is RHCP in the AR bandwidth. The proposed antenna is able to achieve high gain circular polarization in a wide frequency band.

articleTitle: Lens-based Multi-Beam Antenna Technologies for Highly Efficient Dual-Polarized Radiations at Sub-THz Frequencies
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, potential antenna technologies are presented for 6G applications at sub-terahertz frequencies to reduce the propagation loss in the air and dielectric substrates. The proposed work employs a homogeneous uniform lens-based architecture excited by multiple single antenna elements. The feed antennas have simple structures for dual-polarized radiations without implementing any sophisticated microstrip line beamforming circuits to form the directional beams. Numerical simulations by HFSS are presented to validate the concept and demonstrate the feasibility.

articleTitle: The Design of A Single-Layer High-Gain Reflectarray Antenna with Polarization Conversion
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a single-layer high-gain reflectarray antenna with polarization conversion is presented. The proposed reflectarray element consists of a top metallic patch, a dielectric layer and a metallic ground. And the top metallic patch is asymmetric along the x-axis and y-axis, by varying patch size and flipping the top metallic patch 180° along x-axis, full 360° reflected phase coverage with low loss is achieved. Meanwhile, the element has performance of polarization conversion. The polarization of the incident wave and the reflected wave are orthogonal. Furthermore, a 20° offset-fed single-layer high-gain reflectarray with a square aperture is composed by 26 × 26 antenna elements (390 mm × 390 mm) is proposed. The simulated gain is 31.1 dBi @10.0 GHz, and the aperture efficiency is 60.6% @10.0 GHz. The simulated 1-dB and 3-dB gain bandwidth are 14.0% (9.4 GHz – 10.8 GHz) and 23.0% (8.9 GHz – 11.2 GHz) @10.0 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: The Design of An All-Metal Low Profile End-Fire Array Antenna with High Gain
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: An all-metal low profile end-fire array antenna with high gain is proposed in this paper. The proposed antenna consists of a metallic ground, a transmission microstrip line and sixteen pairs of radiating elements. Each element is composed of a horizontal patch and a vertical patch, where the structure of the vertical patch is either rectangular or elliptical. One end of the element is short-circuited to ground, while the other end is connected to the transmission line. The energy from port 1 excites each radiating element along the transmission microstrip line and is finally connected by port 2. The all-metal structure reduces the manufacture difficulty and cost. Finally, the all-metal low profile end-fire array antenna is simulated. Simulated result shows the antenna has a wide bandwidth of 42.1 % in the range of 3.83 GHz to 5.87 GHz and a high gain of 15.0 dBi at 5.0 GHz.

articleTitle: UWB Monopole Antenna Miniaturization and Gain Enhancement using FSS Reflector
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a low profile, wideband, and enhanced flat-gain monopole antenna. The proposed antenna consists of a rectangular radiating element backed by an FSS reflector. This design has a small size of 45 × 50 × 10 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and provides a flat higher gain between 6.8 and 8.1 dBi from 4 to 12 GHz. Moreover, the FSS reflector demonstrates a maximum gain enhancement of 6 dB at 6 GHz due to the effectively in-phase reflection between the antenna and the FSS. Furthermore, a comparison between simulated and measured results is discussed and a comparison with other state-of-the-art antennas is presented.

articleTitle: Frequency Selective Surface Design by Adaptive Artificial Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For the past few decades, through the development and investigation of Frequency Selective Surface (FSS), sensitivity to incident angles is one of the major problems. For traditional methods, to accomplish angle sensitivity, the complexity of FSS cell increase significantly. In this paper, an adaptive Artificial Neural Network (ANN) is proposed to design the FSS cell, which can be efficient for single-layer FSSs. The performance of the design is judged by full-wave simulations of radiation patterns for the entire antenna radome system with and without FSS.

articleTitle: Design & Optimization Procedure of 5G Millimeter-Wave Antenna Integrated in Mobile Devices
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a design and optimization procedure of 5G millimeter-wave (mmWave) antennas integrated in mobile devices. Radiating element’s shape and phase offset between two orthogonal components are investigated, and the study suggests that these parameters can be optimized for wireless performance while complying with RF exposure regulatory. Furthermore, by combining simulations and measurements, regulatory process for commercial mobile devices can be implemented with shorter time, lower cost, and higher effectiveness.

articleTitle: Computer Simulation of 28 GHz Millimeter-wave Propagation in Residential House Environment
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Large-scale computer simulations based on the FDTD techniques with a high-performance computer system are conducted to predict 28 GHz millimeter-wave indoor propagation characteristics in residential house environment. From the calculation results, transient behaviors of received signal power in LOS, NLOS and outdoor are compared with each other. Also, assuming the close-in free space reference distance path loss model, a path loss exponent in LOS is predicted as 1.2. Finally, a diagram comparing the received signal power distribution with the path loss contours is shown.

articleTitle: Gain Enhancement of the Millimeter Wave Radar Sensor Using a Composite Metamaterial Radome
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A composite metamaterial (MTM) radome for 60GHz radar sensor is proposed in this paper. The composite MTM radome consists of two different structures with star and square cells. With those structures, the composite MTM radome can provide gain enhancement for the radar module. The simulated results of the antennas in package (AIP) with the composite MTM radome show a gain improvement more than 3dB compared to that without the radome. Also, measurements have been performed by using a corner reflector at a fix distance and various directions in an anechoic chamber to obtain the level of the received radar signals backscattering from the corner reflector. Good agreements between measurements and simulations are obtained.

articleTitle: Millimeter Wave Antennas Using Gap Waveguides with Beam Steerability at Fixed Frequencies for Beyond 5G Mobile Communications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, we design a 60 GHz millimeter-wave gap waveguide antenna for beam steering applications. Implemented on the premise of a waveguide slot-array, radiated beams can be shone towards designated directions by sliding the pin lattice that makes up one of the walls, thereby altering the modal resonance and thus the phase pattern across the radiating aperture. The array consists of six staggered longitudinal slots. Designs by simulations indicate the ability to steer the main beam through 10 degrees in the elevation plane. The simulated realized gain is 12 dB and the bandwidth is from 54 to 62 GHz (13% fractional bandwidth). The main advantages of this antenna are that it can tailor the main beam with one simple mechanical motion, thereby circumventing the need for complicated electronic networks such as phase shifters, switches or diodes, thus lowering the costs and complexities.

articleTitle: DOA Estimation by Synthetic Aperture Measurement with Compressed Sensing and Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a DOA estimation method by synthetic aperture measurement with neural network and compressed sensing. The proposed method enables to simplify the synthetic aperture measurement by high-resolution of compressed sensing. Additionally, preprocessing technique using synthetic aperture and neural network realizes to reduce computational complexity of compressed sensing. Thus, proposed method is suitable for radio wave environment survey.

articleTitle: Relationships between Mobile Phones’ Metal Exteriors and Millimeter-Wave Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper innovatively presents interesting and inspiring discussions on three relationships between mobile phones’ metal exteriors and millimeter-Wave (mm-Wave) antennas so that the future developments and advances on mm-Wave antennas in the mobile phones can be promisingly enlightened and triggered. The three analyzed relationships involve: (1) the negative one wherein the metal exteriors to mm-Wave antennas are the constraints needed to be overcome, (2) the positive one wherein the metal exteriors to mm-Wave antennas are the contributors able to be utilized, and (3) the combined one wherein the mm-Wave antenna carriers are the extensions of the metal exteriors to benefit the performance of non-mm-Wave antennas in the form of the metal exteriors.

articleTitle: Passive Microwave Electric Field Display with Neon Light Bulb
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: To visualize the electric field distribution is of interest to High Power Microwave (HPM) research. Here we use a panel consists of 3600 6 mm diameter neon bulbs as a field display for a medium power 2.45 GHz source converted from a microwave oven. Commercial EM code with Multi-Level-Fast-Multipole-Method (MLFMM) algorithm is used to simulate the electric field distribution at a short distance. Such display can help decide which mode the microwave source is in.

articleTitle: 5G Millimeter-Wave Eight-Port MIMO Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This work presents an eight-port multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna for fifth generation (5G) millimeter wave (mm-Wave) applications. Each MIMO antenna consists of an inverted T-shaped array with a corporate feed network. The proposed structure is resonating for the 23.5–27.45 GHz band, thus covering the 26 GHz mm-Wave band. Additionally, the peak gain obtained for the MIMO elements is 11.5 dBi. The presented structure provides acceptable values for Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC), and Diversity Gain (DG). The simple structure, high gain, wide bandwidth, and good MIMO performance makes this design suitable for 5G mm-Wave devices.

articleTitle: Microstrip Array Antenna Fed by a Slotted Waveguide
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Balanced, series-fed microstrip array antenna is investigated. The array is consisted of 6 rows of 7 elements and is fed from a narrow wall of the rectangular waveguide, filled with a dielectric material. The array frequency is 10 GHz with bandwidth of 0.7% for SWR = 2. The directivity of the array is 20.7 dBi and its total efficiency is = -0.3 dB. The E-plane and H-plane sidelobes are close to -21 dB. The cross-polarization level in the E-plane and the H-plane is very low.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Planar Frequency Dispersive Phase Shifter for Base Station Antennas
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A frequency-dispersive phase shifter that can be integrated in dual band: 1.5 GHz and 2.0 GHz mobile base station antennas has been proposed to improve communication capacity by increasing the tilt angle of the multiband mobile base station antennas’ low-frequency band. This paper presents the prototype results of the phase shifter by obtaining the simulated and measured S-parameter and transmission phase characteristics.

articleTitle: Analysis of Truncation Error in 3-D Microwave Holographic Imaging
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: For the 3-D microwave holographic imaging algorithm developed in [1], it is found that the reconstructed images suffer from truncation error associating with the finite size of the scanning aperture. In this study, the effect of truncation error is qualitatively discussed and quantified with a series of simulated results. Referring to our defined quantified values, the criterion of feasible range which guarantees an acceptable error level is proposed.

articleTitle: A Dual-polarized Wideband Reconfigurable Reflected / Transmitted Filter Array Antenna Element
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a dual-polarized wideband reconfigurable reflected/ transmitted filter array antenna element is proposed. The proposed array element consists of three metallic layers and two substrates. Top and bottom metallic layers are designed as square patches with same size, and the middle layer is set as a metallic square-ring slot, where four controllable switches are loaded symmetrically on the square-ring slot. By altering the ON or OFF of four controllable switches, the element can achieve the reconfiguration in the reflection and transmission state. Meanwhile, the element adopts symmetrical structure to realize dual polarization characteristics and has a wideband performance due to its frequency selective surface structure. The simulated results demonstrate that the frequency band of –0.9 dB reflection magnitude and –1.5 dB transmission magnitude both ranges from 8 GHz to 12 GHz.

articleTitle: A Compact and Flexible Dual-Band Antenna for Near-Body Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A compact and flexible dual-band antenna for near-body Internet of things (IoT) applications is presented. Modified Inverted F-antenna (IFA) structure is employed as to allow dual-band operation. Two thin films of Polycarbonate (PC) and Polyurethane (PU) are used in order to provide flexibility to the structure. The antenna covers incoming lower 5G (n18) and 915-MHz industrial, scientific and medical (ISM) bands and exhibits a maximum gain of -8.78 dBi. Moreover, antenna matching is insensitive to near body influence.

articleTitle: Mantle Cloak Antenna Using Strip Conductors for Mutual Coupling Reduction at Frequency Lower Than Operating Frequency
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a mantle cloak antenna using strip conductors for mutual coupling reduction at a lower frequency than the antenna’s operating frequency is proposed. As a result, by using the strip conductors locating around the surface of a dielectric substrate, the mutual coupling of the mantle cloak antenna at 720 MHz can be reduced, and the antenna characteristics of the antenna can be maintained at 750 MHz simultaneously.

articleTitle: One Layer of Reflectarray Antenna Changing Beam Direction by Polarization
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Reflectarray antenna applies the reflection phase control function of a metal loaded frequency selective reflector to a reflector antenna, It is possible to control the reflection phases of vertical (V) and horizontal (H) polarization with a single reflectarray if the shape and arrangement of the elements are appropriately designed In this study, we investigate a high-precision reflectarray using three linear elements in a single-layer structure. The results of the analysis demonstrate that the mutual coupling between the H and V components is reduced, and the effect of manufacturing error is minimized. Consequently, it is inferred that the beam can be emitted in different directions for each polarization.

articleTitle: In-Band Full-Duplex Propagation-Domain Techniques and Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In-band full-duplex (IBFD) systems can suppress their consequential self-interference (SI) using a combination of cancellation techniques. Approaches within the propagation domain represent the first opportunity to reduce the SI, and help enable subsequent methods in the analog and digital domains of a transceiver. This paper summarizes these important propagation-domain techniques in the context of passive, active and antenna interface categories for both shared and multiple antenna scenarios. Additionally, IBFD applications that leverage these techniques to create novel multi-function systems are discussed, including a vehicle-to-everything concept and military operations.

articleTitle: A Highly Compact and Highly Efficient Huygens Antenna Array
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A highly compact and highly efficient Huygens 1 × 4 antenna array is reported in this paper. The Huygens array consists of two major parts: a TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.5,0</inf> mode SIW waveguide with seamlessly integrated phase inverters and two folded L-shaped metallic plates being orthogonally connected to it. Four magnetic dipoles are formed on the radiating aperture of the waveguide while four electric dipoles are realized on the plates. Their moments are orthogonal to each other and naturally in phase. Thus, Huygens cardioid radiation patterns are realized. The system operates around 10 GHz. It has a 7.7% simulated overlapped –10-dB impedance and 3-dB realized gain bandwidth from 9.44 to 10.2 GHz, 760 MHz. The peak realized gain value is 10.23 dBi within this bandwidth. The realized gain pattern at 10 GHz has a narrow (25°) half-power beamwidth (HPBW) in the H-plane (ϕ = 0°) and a wide (152°) HPBW in the E-plane (ϕ = 90°). The aperture efficiency of the array reaches 97.5%.

articleTitle: Implementation of 8 Channels Phase Conjugation on FPGA for Microwave Power Transmission
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a phase conjugation (PC) system for 8 channels microwave power transmission (MPT) application, operating at the frequency band 2.45 GHz, using a field programmable gate array (FPGA) and high-speed analog to digital converter (ADC) and digital to analog converter (DAC). PC algorithm is implemented using some digital logics on the FPGA and a small size buffer is used for data acquisition. In addition, in order to operate the MPT system at 2.45 GHz, an appropriate frequency planning of ADC and DAC is proposed. Typical type of patch antennas is used to verify the implemented system and from the measurement results, it works well as the MPT application.

articleTitle: A Multiband LTE/WWAN Antenna Design for Tablet and Laptop Devices
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a multiband antenna design applicable for tablet and laptop devices. The antenna operating bands are formed with five resonant modes and cover extensive mobile communication bands, including GSM850/900, GSM1800/1900, UMTS, and LTE2300/2500. These bands are often referred to as LTE low and high bands. The proposed antenna geometry comprises three elements. A closed slot is placed on the metal ground. A U-shaped feeding line and an Lshaped microstrip line are printed on an FR4 substrate. The Ushaped feeding line excites the resonance mode of the closed slot. The L-shaped microstrip line provides an alternative resonant path for multiband operations. The resonant mechanism of each band is examined. Simulation results show that the proposed multiband antenna has good impedance matching and high radiation efficiency in the desired LTE/WWAN bands.

articleTitle: A V-band Array Antenna Made of Liquid Crystal Polymer
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: We present a V-band array antenna operating from 57 to 71 GHz using liquid crystal polymer (LCP). In order to achieve a wide beamforming range in the horizontal direction only and a relatively high gain, a sub-array antenna consisting of four patches arranged in a row is applied. Each sub-array antenna is fed from the center in order to prevent changing of the radiation direction when frequency changes. The layer structure with LCP substrate consists of wiring layer, ground, antenna layer, and parasitic antenna layer from the bottom. Measurement shows that S11 is less than -10 dB and gain is higher than 9 dBi in range from 57 to 71 GHz.

articleTitle: A Low Profile UWB Antenna on a Large Flat Conductor
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel low-profile MS feed UWB antenna on a large flat conductor. It is first time to reduce the distance between antenna and conductor by introducing slots in the conductor. The designed distance is 0.04 λwhich is a quarter of some existing results. Simulated results show the antenna has a bandwidth of 167.6% from 1.55 GHz to 17.6 GHz with S11 below -10 dB and the peak gain is large than 6 dBi during a frequency range of 2 GHz to 17 GHz.

articleTitle: Reception Characteristics Improvement by Polarization MIMO Gap-filler on Long-distance Transmission in Terrestrial TV Broadcasting
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, effects of surrounding buildings and the T<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> - R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf> distance on reception quality in terrestrial broadcasting is examined. Numerical results show that the reception quality can be improved by polarization MIMO Gap-filler. It is also show that hight distribution of buildings has large effect on reception quality.

articleTitle: A Broadband Reflectarray Based on Multi-Resonance Unit
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, a wide-band microstrip reflectarray unit based on a three-resonance structure has been proposed. The simulation results show that the unit can achieve nearly parallel phase characteristic curves within a wide frequency band, and the phase change range at the center frequency exceeds 800º. Based on the units proposed, a 77-element reflectarray was designed. The simulated results indicate that the reflectarray has a 1-dB (9.61-14.61 GHz) of 41.3%, and the highest radiation efficiency of the reflectarray antenna is 64.3%.

articleTitle: Tunable Huygens' Transmission Metasurface on Double-Layer PCB
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A tunable transmission Huygens' metasurface implemented in compact double-layer PCB is presented. The unit cells consist of electric and magnetic dipoles where the phase responses are independently controlled by an off-the-shelf PIN diode and varactors, respectively. The DC bias lines are embedded in double metallic layers and highly resistive resistors and DC blocking capacitors are used to reduce cell-to-cell and RF-DC coupling. The metasurface unit cell structures are designed for proof of concept at 10 GHz. For efficient transmission with multiple phases, the optimum pairs of ON-OFF states of the PIN diode and capacitance of the varactors are investigated. The final unit cells with electronic tuning cover transmission phase states from -90°to +150° with average loss of -3 dB.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Microstrip Array Antenna Fed by Cavity Slots
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A `dual-polarized microstrip array antenna with 6x2 elements is investigated. The antenna is matched for 9.5 to 10.2 GHz for VSWR = 2 (bandwidth 7%). The directivity of the antenna is 16.7 dBi with total efficiency -0.1 dB. The mutual coupling between neighbor elements is lower than -40 dB and the cross-polarization level is lower than -60 dB.

articleTitle: On Effective Parameter for Human Motion Recognition with MW-MIMO Radar Using CNN
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Radar-based Human Motion Recognition (HMR) has been expected to be applied to home security and human monitoring. We have been studying 2-D motion imaging using features such as Doppler frequency, range and Direction of Arrival (DOA), and the recognition of motion imaging maps using machine learning. In this paper, 10 motions observed using Millimeter-Wave Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MW-MIMO) radar are shown in 6 types of 2-D maps in above domains. We evaluated the HMR accuracy in each map using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and clarified effective parameters for realizing highly accurate HMR.

articleTitle: Compact Circularly Polarized Disc Patch Antenna Designed with Sector Mushroom Structures
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A new compact circularly polarized (CP) disc patch antenna is designed with sector mushroom structures operating at 3.5GHz. The disc antenna is made from low permittivity dielectrics but featured with an electrically small patch with a diameter of 0.41λg, which is beyond the 0.58λg limitation for a conventional patch antenna. The relative -10dB impendence bandwidth for the new antenna is 6.5% while the 3dB axial ratio bandwidth is 1.5%. Moreover the metamaterial antenna has a peak CP gain of 5.9dBic. These performances can meet the demand of mobile communication application at 3.5GHz.

articleTitle: A Printed-Inverted F Antenna Combined with Two L-Shaped Elements for Dual Band Circular Polarization
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Authors have proposed a printed inverted-F antenna (IFA) for dual-band dual-sense circular polarization. In this paper, a printed IFA combined with two L-shaped elements for dual-band circular polarization. The proposed antenna radiates same sense circular polarization in two frequency bands. The relationship between the antenna characteristics (return loss, axial ratio, and gain) and the additional L-shaped elements are discussed. The bandwidth of 10dB-return loss with a 3dB-axial ratio are 4.6% and 7.6% in the lower and higher frequency bands. The antenna size is relatively small.

articleTitle: A Solution for Simulation of the Electrically Large Reflectarray
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a solution for the full-wave simulation of the electrically large reflectarray employing the concept of ‘element-in-array pattern’ and near field source technique which is supported in commercial EM software. This solution is capable of calculating the radiation pattern of reflectarray of any size illuminated by arbitrary horn working at from millimeter wave to terahertz. A numerical example has proved its accuracy.

articleTitle: Antenna-in-Packages for Array Modularization at Millimeter-wave Frequencies and its Applications in 5G O-RAN
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this paper, the design issues of antenna-in-package (AiP) is discussed to modularize arrays at millimeter-wave (mmW) frequencies for 5G applications. The current progress of AiP technologies at NTU is also summarized. The issues of considerations include different fabrication process, dielectric property deviation and mechanical limitations to realize the antenna structure. Antenna designs for various applications, ranging from user equipment, CPE to small cell BTS antennas, have been developed at different sizes. The radiation characteristics of these AiPs will be presented to demonstrate the behaviors of AiPs using these processes. Both full-wave simulations and experimental measurements will be presented to validate the AiP designs.

articleTitle: Realization of an 110GHz Antenna Array Module by Using AiP Technologies for Potential 6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Sub-Terahertz frequencies are potential bands for 6G applications. Due to the small wavelengths, antenna-in-package (AiP) technologies will be used to realize the antenna system for compactness and low dielectric losses. This paper presents an AiP design at 110 GHz for potential 6G applications. The target is to examine the behaviors of currently available dielectric substrates and fabrication mechanical process. Numerical full-wave simulations are performed to design an array of 8 8× elements to exhibit the basic characteristics.

articleTitle: Development of MACKEY II type M miniaturized using multiple slits
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A meta-surface-inspired antenna chip developed by KIT EOE Laboratory (MACKEY), which can operate in free space and on a metal plate, was investigated in this study. We propose a method to reduce the size of MACKEY II for the 920 MHz band to that of a card.

articleTitle: Low-Frequency Electromagnetic Characterization of Layered Media Using Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: The problem of determining the dielectric properties and thickness of materials using electromagnetic waves can be found in different geophysical applications. In such scenarios, a radiating source is placed on the top interface, and a receiver is moved along a preferred direction to measure the electromagnetic fields. In this work, we have considered such a scenario with low-frequency electromagnetic waves. We have trained a deep neural network to learn the complex relationship between the field values and substrate thickness and dielectric constants. Then we have used that network to estimate these quantities from field value measurements. The results show very low mean absolute percentage errors for both noise-free and noisy training data as long as the noise level of the test data is not too high. A successful realization of the proposed method can help monitor the characteristics of geophysical substances like glacier, sea ice etc.

articleTitle: Ultra Wide Band Dual-Feed Millimeter Wave Antenna
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Faster data throughput and low latency are the main development agenda in modern communication system. In addition to higher modulation rate, mm Wave also can achieve high data throughput, low latency and significance of results. In this paper, Ultra Wide Band Dual polarized Antenna is designed for post 5th Generation Wireless communications that can support n257 (25.6GHZ-29.5GHz), n258 (24.25GHZ-27.5GHz), n260(37GHz-40GHz) and n261 (27.5GHz-28.35GHz). Ultra wideband is limited to have higher antenna gain, however, antenna array design can improve antenna gain and radiation pattern, one dual feed antenna can provide two antenna radiation patterns,Antenna gain degradation by the tolerance of material can be improved by high power laser beam. The antenna covers 24.24 GHż29.5 GHz and 37 GHz~40 GHz and has a broad bandwidth both in low and high band frequency. The peak gain of high band frequency is 5.5dB and the peak gain of low band is 5.1 dB. The dimension of the antenna element can achieve as small size as of 10 mm x 10mm x1.844mm, and the size is suitable for mm Wave repeater application and mobile phone with mm Wave function.

Author Keywords: Ultra Wide Band Monopole with Reflector

articleTitle: Room Geometry Estimation based Device-Free Localization Method
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In recent years, IoT and AI technologies have been developing rapidly. To utilize these technologies in home environment, it is important to capture and visualize environmental information in a house. Previous study has developed an indoor device-free localization (DFL) method using multipath radio tomographic imaging (RTI) based on emerging millimeter-wave (mm-wave) radio systems such as 5 G mobile and IEEE 802.11 ad/ay WiGig. The multipath RTI requires the prior knowledge about the individual propagation pathways of the targeted environment instead of constructing the measurement based dictionary. In this paper, the localization method using the room geometry estimation technique to obtain the necessary prior knowledge was proposed, and the performance was demonstrated via ray tracing simulations.

articleTitle: Dual-Polarized Antenna Array Modularization by LTCC Process at Millimeter Wave Frequencies for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A broadband antenna array module is presented for 5G CPE applications, which was fabricated by low temperature co-fired ceramic (LTCC) for 5G base station or customer premise equipment (CPE) applications. The antenna elements are dual-polarized along +/-45 degrees to avoid the harmful multi-path effects from metal supporting structures. They are in a cross-dipole architecture with tapered shapes to improve bandwidth, which were designed on multi-layered dielectric substrates to produce a bandwidth larger than 4 GHz from the full-wave simulations with good isolation.

articleTitle: Wideband MIMO Antenna for 5G Smartphone Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: In this letter, we presented a multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) antenna system with wideband performance for 5G smartphone applications. Firstly, a planar inverted-F antenna (PIFA) is designed to born a monopole-like mode. Secondly, an inverted-T shaped open slot is etched in PIFA to generate a loop mode and a slot mode. As a result, the antenna-element realizes a wide bandwidth of 83 % ranging from 3.3 to 8 GHz with a size of 14 × 7 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Finally, eight such antenna-elements are arranged as an 8 × 8 MIMO antenna system. The simulated results show that the proposed antenna system has promising performances.

articleTitle: RF Front-end of ISDB-T Receiver for High Mobility Applications
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This article presents a RF front-end of receiver for ISDB-T applications. The proposed RF front-end of receiver explores to consist of use a divided by 48 pulse swallow dividers and single-stage of low noise amplifier (LNA) with Gm-C bandpass filter using series-peaking design for ISDB-T and DTV with receiving sensitivity of high mobility applications.

articleTitle: Band-Notched Reconfigurable Ultra-wideband Antenna Based on Square Ring Slot
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a band-notched reconfigurable ultra-wideband antenna based on square ring slot. By adding two ellipatical patches around the 3×3 circular metasurface, the working bandwidth of the antenna is effectively expanded. Through arranging two sets of square ring slots on the rectangular ground plane, notched band within the ultra-wideband is emerged. Furthermore, adjusting the on-off state of the eight PIN diodes in the square ring slot, the antenna realizes reconfigurable notched band. The results show that the -10 dB bandwidth of the antenna ranges from 3.5 GHz to 8 GHz, and five band-notched modes are realized at 3.5 GHz, 4.7 GHz, 5.1 GHz, 6.2 GHz and 7.2 GHz.

articleTitle: Metamaterial Minkowski Fractal Antenna With Defective Ground Structure
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper explores two metamaterial fractal antenna (MFA), in which one has complete ground plane and other uses defective ground structure (DGS) with square split ring resonator (SSR) are designed for 5G applications. The radiating layer of both antennas based on first iteration of minkowski fractal structure with complimentary split ring resonator (CSSR). The proposed antennas are simulated using CST microwave studio. The MFA with complete ground plane/DGS is operating between 3.48GHz-3.52GHz and 3.3GHz-3.7GHz, respectively. Both antennas show an excellent gain of 5.1dB and 4.5dB, respectively. The results show that MFA with DGS structure has an excellent bandwidth improvement with good gain, which can be an ideal candidate for 5G application.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Wideband Design of Vivaldi-type antenna for multi-communication applications at millimeter wave frequencies
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposed a balanced antipodal Vivaldi antenna (BAVA), which improved the squinted radiation patterns of BAVA and retaining its cross-polarization levels. We asymmetric discarding the substrate between the metal fins to adjust the beam direction making the beam squint smaller, and etched some slots on both fins to extend the lower-end bandwidth and improve the radiation directivity. The proposed design operates over 19-84GHz with return loss < -10dB and present a maximum gain of 13.09 dB at 48GHz. Numerical assessments to validate the proposed antenna design are conducted.

articleTitle: Dual-Band Circularly Polarized Helical Antenna for Satellite Buoy
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper proposes a new type of dual-band four-arm helical antenna. The bands used in this research are 1.575 GHz and 2.4 GHz. The band of 1.575 GHz is for GPS, and the band of 2.4 GHz is for WLAN. The helical antenna be made of four metal arms with a phase difference of 90° and good electrical conductivity. Here we proposes that the phase difference of 90 ° causes the circular polarization by the network analyzer. In the past, the helical antennas are for a single band. The characteristics of the helical antenna in this paper, are dual bands and circular polarization. In the future, design the feeding network to achieve the propose of adjustable left-hand circular polarization and right-hand circular polarization.

articleTitle: Detection of Defective Elements in Array Antennas Using Artificial Neural Networks and Eigenmode Currents
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: A method for finding defective elements in array antennas is introduced. The method is named as ANN-EC because the method is based on an artificial neural network (ANN) and eigenmode currents (EC). Current distribution of the array antennas is reconstructed from magnitude of their near-field using the ANN-EC. The ANN-EC is applied to dipole array antennas including defective elements. It is demonstrated that defective elements in the array antennas can be found successfully using the ANN-EC.

articleTitle: Shorted Four-Element Patch Antenna with High Directivity and Wideband for Small Metal-Tag
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: This paper presents a miniaturized tag for UHF RFID applications which provided a simple mechanism to tune the impedance match at the desired frequency and extended the bandwidth of the proposed electrically small tag antenna on a metallic object. The compact tag antenna is configured by the four-element radiating patchs and a separated ground plane, which was connected through the four via pins and excited by a feed in the middle of the two 100 Ω microstrip lines. To match the complex input impedance of a UCODE 8/8m chip, the tag antennas’ impedance was controlled by the four radiating edges of the rectangular patches. Besides, dividing a ground plane into two small ground plates significantly enhanced the directivity pattern and radiation efficiency of the small tag. The optimized prototype dimensions of 30.01 × 30.01 × 3.12 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> (0.092 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.092 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.0098 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>) yielded a reading distance of 8.5 m, the high radiation efficiency of 38%, and a wide bandwidth of 40 MHz, which covers a spectrum of 26 MHz of North America band (902 – 928 MHz).

articleTitle: Influence of Mutual Coupling and Surrounding Objects on Base Station Antennas in ITS
publicationTitle: 2021 International Symposium on Antennas and Propagation (ISAP)
abstract: Adaptive arrays which reduce interference are being considered ITS (Intelligent Transport Systems) base stations to realize automatic driving and safe driving support [1]. However, adaptive pattern control capability of the system may be degraded due to the mutual coupling between elements and the influence of surrounding objects. In this paper, the effects of mutual coupling between elements and surrounding objects on the adaptive arrays are clarified, and the appropriate base station antenna configuration is investigated. As a result of analysis, it is confirmed that the effect of mutual coupling between elements on the adaptive arrays is small. It is also confirmed that the distance, position, and size of the surrounding objects had a significant effect on the adaptive array.
